item.content:encoded: TUSCALOOSA, ALABAMA - NOVEMBER 9: Amari Allen #5 of the Alabama Crimson Tide shoots a first half three against the Oakland Golden Grizzlies at Coleman Coliseum on November 9, 2026 in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. (Photo by Brandon Sumrall/Getty Images) | Getty Images Alabama hosted Seton Hall on Friday night at Coleman Coliseum and had to hold on to win 82-76. Bama improved to 4-0 with the win while the Pirates fell to 3-1. The Tide started fast, then slowed down, then poured it on, before slipping at the end and letting the visitors back in the game. Coach Nate Oats used a starting lineup consisting of Amari Allen, Aden Holloway, London Jamison, Drew Fielder, and Brandon Garrison. Seton Hall coach Shaheen Holloway sent out Simeon Welcher, Mihailo Welcher, Elijah Fisher, Devin Williams, and Roddie Anderson III for the open tip. Garrison quickly scored down low for a 2-0 lead, Fielder hit 2-3 free throws and Allen knocked down a three for a 7-2 lead with 17:40 left in the half. Holloway hit from deep, followed by Fielder and Allen both making a pair of free throws for a 14-6 lead with 14:46 on the clock. With 8:17 remaining in the stanza Seton Hall took the lead a 18-17. Allen hit from three again to regain the lead before the Pirates grabbed a 28-22 lead at the 4:58 mark. The Tide went on a 16-0 run to close the half, led by Allen. Holloway got in the lane and contorted his body to knock down a floater as time ran out in the period, giving Bama the 38-28 lead a the break. Alabama shot 11-30 for 37% in the half, including 4-13 for 31% from deep. Bama made 12-15 at the free throw line for 80%. The Tide had 29 rebounds with 11 of them being offensive. After tying a school record with 30 assists in their last game, Bama could only manage four first half assists, to go with four blocks, two steals, and commited 12 turnovers. Allen was the big gun with 18 points, helped by 3-3 from deep, while adding two rebounds, an assist, and a block. Holloway scored seven points and made his only three point shot. Allen and Holloway were 4-4 combined from three while the rest of their teammates combined to go 0-9. Garrison played well down low with four points, six rebounds, and an assist. Seton Hall was 12-36 for 33%, 2-12 from three for 17%, and made 2-2 at the free throw line. The Pirates had only 15 rebounds with six offensively, with seven assists, three blocks, seven steals, and gave the ball away five times. Ilya Dolinski led the team with eight points, followed by Trey Parker with five. Bama sent out the same starting five for the second half, and kept the scoring steak alive, reaching 20 in a row before Seton Hall scored. Garrison notched the first two baskets of the period, and the Tide had built a lead of 42-28. Allen and Cole Cloer both hit a pair of free throws and Jemsion knocked down a three for his only basket of the game and with 17:20 left the Tide led 49-32. The lead hovered around 12-15 points up until the 14:55 mark when Garrison was called for a technical foul-for some unknown reason. With 12 minutes left the Pirates had closed to within 11 points at 57-46. Seton Hall kept on punching (sometimes literally)and stayed within striking distance. With 6:51 left a three pointer by SH closed the margin to six at 66-60. Holloway hit a pair of freebies and Cloer knocked down down a three !!!!- from the top of the key for a 71-60 lead with 5:45 left. The lead was 11 with 3:58 on the clock, but an 0-5 stretch at the free throw line by Bama tightened things up. The Pirates made the score 77-71 with 1:21 left, and then 77-74 with 55 seconds left. The Tide finally got the ball in Holloways hands and the senior made 4-4 at the stripe to close about the game with an 82-76 victory for the home team. In the second half Bama shot 12-23 for 52%, 3-8 for 38% from three, and 17-23 for 74% at the free throw line. Overall the Tide finished 23-53 for 43%, 7-21 for 33% from behind the arc, and 29-38 for 76% at the free throw line. Alabama totaled 41 rebounds, 14 offensive , 11 assists, seven blocks, eight steals, and 17 turnovers. Allen played a season high 33 minutes and scored 24 points on 6-10 shooting with three rebounds, five assists, and two steals. Holloway had a season high 18 points, buoyed by 8-8 shooting at the line, in a team high 35 minutes. Cloer had his best game scoring 12 points with five rebounds in 23 minutes. Interestingly other than Cloer all the freshmen players had their minutes severely cut. Tarris Bouie played only four minutes, Qayden Samuels garnered 10 minutes, Anderson Diaz saw eight minutes of action, while Jaxon Richardson played 11 minutes- with most being in crunch time. Oats said after the game that Cloer “is about the right stuff” and Richardson was giving a lot of effort rebounding and defending, and if you do that you will play more. Seton Hall was 14-33 for 42% including 5-14 from three and 15-16 on free throws in the second half. Overall the Pirates hit 26-69 for 38%, 7-26 for 27% from three and 17-18 for 94% on free throws. SH crashed the boards in he second half and finished with 36 total with 16 on the offensive end. The Pirates had 13 assists, five blocks, eight steals, and committed 12 turnovers. Dolinski led the team with 15 points and added five rebounds. Elijah Fisher had 14 points, five rebounds and, three assists, and two steals. Parker finished with 12 and Williamson had 10 points, seven rebounds, and blocked four shots. This game was a step up in competition for the Tide, but this game shouldn’t have been this close. The Pirates mucked things up, playing hard and very physical. After a fantastic shooting game against Oakland on Monday, the shots were not falling tonight. Allen and Holloway took over and made sure the Tide would not lose. Garrison had a nice game going until he got in foul trouble. Cloer and Richardson contributed their best games of their young Alabama careers. With all that being said the team did what they had to do to win, when not playing at their best. Next up is a homecoming for Antoine Pettway and his Kennesaw State team. Pettway, the head man at KSU will come back to his Alma mater Tuesday night for a 6 p.m. CT game, The SEC Network Plus will have the broadcast. RollTide

item.title: Lionel Messi to return to Estadio Monumental on January 19 as Inter Miami face River Plate in historic Buenos Aires preseason friendly
item.description: FBL-MLS-INTER MIAMI-CHARLOTTE CF - AFP Inter Miami captain Lionel Messi will return to the Estadio Monumental on January 19 when the Major League Soccer side face River Plate in a preseason friendly. The Buenos Aires exhibition will mark the first time the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner has ever played a club match on Argentine soil. Argentine icon makes homeland return Announced on the Argentine club's social media channels , January's fixture brings Messi back to the venue where he made 29 appearances for his country. His last outing there came on October 6 during a 3-0 win over Benin that marked his 208th and final international cap alongside his 126th goal. Before that farewell, hosts president Stefano Di Carlo handed him an honorary membership card, plaque and named shirt . Previous meetings span four clubs That October tribute also referenced December 18, 2022, when the playmaker led his nation to a third World Cup crown to sit alongside his 2021 and 2024 Copa America triumphs across a 21-year international career. Although January's trip is his maiden club appearance in his homeland, the forward has previously faced opposition from his native country on four occasions elsewhere. Representing Barcelona, he beat Estudiantes at the 2009 Club World Cup in the United Arab Emirates before facing Marcelo Gallardo's side - who boast 38 domestic titles and four Copa Libertadores crowns - in the December 2015 final in Japan. Under Luis Enrique, the Catalans won 3-0 as their talisman opened the scoring in the 36th minute prior to a second-half Luis Suarez brace, while he also defeated Boca Juniors in the 2018 Joan Gamper Trophy and drew 1-1 with boyhood club Newell's Old Boys in Florida in 2024. Herons build around prolific talisman Since joining the Herons in 2023 and extending his contract through the 2028 campaign , the veteran has guided the franchise to the 2023 Leagues Cup and 2024 Supporters' Shield. In September 2026, he became the first player in club history to reach 100 goals before clinching a record second consecutive Golden Boot with 26 regular-season strikes. Earlier this week, the forward was also named a finalist for the 2026 league MVP award as he bids to become the first player to claim the prize three years running. Adding a fixture in the Argentine capital continues an international preseason strategy that has previously seen the American outfit visit Peru, Ecuador, Colombia and Puerto Rico. Star-studded squad prepares for kickoff While kickoff times and ticket details remain unconfirmed, Miami expect Casemiro, Rodrigo De Paul, Suarez, Nicolas Otamendi and Thiago Almada to join their skipper for the trip. The match will help River prepare for their domestic schedule while serving as a high-profile warm-up for the visitors. Following their South American visit, the Herons will open the 2027 league campaign against FC Cincinnati at Nu Stadium on February 19.

item.title: Matt Henry's three-ball demolition exposes India's batting frailties ahead of 2027 ODI World Cup
item.description: Three balls. That was all Matt Henry needed to turn India’s chase of 334 into a rout. Henry was only supposed to be passing through. Having missed most of the T20Is with a leg injury and the early ODIs amid concussion concerns after colliding with Devon Conway, the seamer stayed back at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui simply to prove his fitness and get some overs into his legs before the Tests. Instead, he produced one of the most devastating opening overs in ODI cricket, reducing India to 0/3 and setting up a 244-run thrashing — India’s second-biggest defeat by runs in the format. India collapsed for 89 and the contest was effectively sealed before the visitors had even troubled the scorers. Henry’s first ball landed on a good length on off, kicked, and seamed away just enough to square up Rohit Sharma and kiss the outside edge on its way to first slip. It was a jarring sight, painfully reminiscent of the twilight of Rohit’s Test career and an increasingly familiar one when he faces quality fast bowling in overseas conditions. Next up was Virat Kohli. Henry pitched fuller, drew him forward and beat the outside edge by inches. Three balls later, he wobbled the seam from an identical spot. This one nipped back in, stayed low and rattled Kohli’s stumps. Then came Shreyas Iyer, walking out for his captaincy debut and walking back with a golden duck — the first Indian skipper to suffer that fate. Trapped on the crease by one that darted past his inside edge, Iyer fell to a DRS review while Henry was already mid-celebration. India’s first run came off the 17th delivery of the innings. For anyone watching, it was impossible not to be dragged back to Old Trafford in July 2019, when Henry’s 3/37 ripped the heart out of India’s World Cup semifinal chase. Seven years on, the scars remain wide open. With the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa looming, where conditions could offer similar bounce and seam movement, this rout should set off alarm bells. A hint of lateral movement was all it took to expose India’s glaring technical chinks. To be fair, Henry was not operating in isolation. Kyle Jamieson used his height to extract extra bounce and movement, getting Ruturaj Gaikwad (5) to edge a feeble push outside off to second slip as India slipped to 9 for 4. Ishan Kishan (27 off 53) and Axar Patel (21 off 36) briefly resisted with a 44-run stand. Naman Dhir (21 off 24) muscled two sixes, but Matt Fisher (3 for 31) kept hitting hard lengths at high pace to snuff out any fight. Henry then returned to clean up the tail, finishing with career-best ODI figures. If India’s batting was brittle, the thinking off the field was equally baffling. On a surface offering genuine seam and bounce, leaving Mohammed Siraj out of the XI again defied cricketing logic. Gautam Gambhir’s selection calls continue to puzzle, raising serious questions about the roadmap ahead. Cruelly for India, they had walked into the innings break believing they held the momentum. Dropped twice on 5 off Auqib Nabi in the second over of New Zealand’s innings, Young cashed in with a career-best 125 off 108 balls. Alongside Finn Allen (41 off 30), he took down Kuldeep Yadav (0 for 73 in 8 overs) in a 90-run fourth-wicket stand before Rohit redeemed an earlier dropped chance with a sharp diving catch at short cover. Part-timer Naman Dhir then removed Young and took a diving catch to dismiss Michael Bracewell off Gurnoor Brar. Axar (2 for 39) and Arshdeep Singh, who removed Mitchell Santner, helped India take 6 for 77 in the final 13.1 overs and bowl New Zealand out for 333. New Zealand, trailing 2-1, now head into Sunday’s final ODI without Henry and Jamieson, both bound for Test duty.

item.title: What Tommy Lloyd and Caleb Holt said after Arizona’s win over Auburn
item.description: AUBURN, ALABAMA - NOVEMBER 13: Caleb Holt #3 of the Arizona Wildcats dribbles the ball as Kolby King #4 of the Auburn Tigers defends during the first half of an NCAA basketball game at Neville Arena on November 13, 2026 in Auburn, Alabama. (Photo by Stew Milne/Getty Images) | Getty Images Playing in front of approximately 150 family and friends, Alabama native Caleb Holt had one thing on his mind Friday night. “I just wanted to go out there and win at the end of the day,“ Holt said. Arizona’s star freshman guard did just that, scoring a career-best 24 points to lead the Wildcats to an 80-69 road victory at Auburn. Winning on the road anywhere is hard. but especially at Auburn, which hadn’t lost a home nonconference game since 2016. That was also the year Arizona last won a true road game at an SEC school, when it beat Mizzou. Arizona’s victory over Auburn moves the Wildcats to 3-1 on the year. Here’s what Tommy Lloyd and Holt said after the win. Lloyd on Holt’s performance and his overall progress: “An incredibly mature performance for a 19-year-old guy. To come back home and and to play the way he did. When we landed yesterday, thank God there were flights so we got here on the plane, and we came to the gym and shot a little bit. And I kind of peeked down, nothing crazy, and I saw Caleb shoot a few balls. I’m like, ‘Oh, it’s pretty tight.‘ It felt good. I had a good feeling about how he was going to come out today. The great thing about about Caleb is his best days are ahead of him. I think he’s a really unique player. He’s just this ferocious competitor and has this bundle of energy and we’re trying to help him harness it and find his way at a sophisticated high level basketball with it. He really wants to learn. So to me, that gives this guy a really high ceiling. It’s a joy to coach him every day. He’s grateful and he’s he’s fun to be around. He wants to deliver for his teammates, and that makes him special.” On what Arizona did defensively to close out the win: “I think we just kind of hung in there. (That) was the biggest thing. And I think we were able to get Mo back on the floor, which really helped. It’s one of those situations where playing on the road is tough. Obviously, this is a tough place to play, and so anytime you can get a lead and then make a little bit of a run to extend your lead, not that you’re gonna let them try to make a run back, but you know it’s coming. You’re so much more comfortable, even as that lead’s dwindling a little bit, that you know if you take a breath and you can put together two or three possessions in a row and build your lead back up, it’s really important on the road to do that. Like, hey, our first game of the year, obviously we didn’t play good against a good UCLA team, and we got down and we were battling back all game, and then we had to make the run to come back. So to me, that gives this guy a really high ceiling. It’s a joy to coach him every day. He’s grateful and he’s he’s fun to be around. He wants to deliver for his teammates, and that makes him special.” On what Arizona did defensively to close out the win: “I think we just kind of hung in there. (That) was the biggest thing. And I think we were able to get Mo back on the floor, which really helped. It’s one of those situations where playing on the road is tough. Obviously, this is a tough place to play, and so anytime you can get a lead and then make a little bit of a run to extend your lead, not that you’re gonna let them try to make a run back, but you know it’s coming. You’re so much more comfortable, even as that lead’s dwindling a little bit, that you know if you take a breath and you can put together two or three possessions in a row and build your lead back up, it’s really important on the road to do that. Like, hey, our first game of the year, obviously we didn’t play good against a good UCLA team, and we got down and we were battling back all game, and then we had to make the run to come back. Then sometimes you make that run to come back, and you just take a little bit of a breath, and it feels like the team that was ahead makes a run again, and that that was just the case tonight. So we were fortunate.” On Auburn’s team and how they challenged Arizona: “I think they’re good. Obviously Keyshawn Hall was a problem at that four spot with his skill.I think they’ve kind of got more shooting this year, and just I’m telling you, those big fellas are a problem. To be able to have two of them and kind of roll them out there, I think it really impacted us early. Ivan didn’t play his best game till towards later in the second half when closing time. But I think they got a few of his shots, and it was kind of surprising. The big fella has six blocks. It’s game changing. So they had, what, 13 blocks total. That’s going to be interesting to see how that evolves over the course of this year. It’s hard to play against.” On going with a tighter lineup: “We felt like this was a really important game for our season, no it’s a must-win situation in game four. But we knew coming here, I’m expecting it to be a quad one win. This team’s trying to establish its identity and kind of build our confidence. I I tightened the lineup today, changed the starting lineup because I wanted to put a little bit more ball handling out on the court, and that lineup has been our best lineup. Sometimes you start it, you fall into six or eight more minutes a game of it and we kind of opened with that lineup and we were able to close with that lineup. So the guys off the bench came in and made their impact. But there’s no doubt, I mean our bench is going to have to develop over the course of this season. Just maybe today wasn’t the day you know to to go deep and give them long runs.” On Bryce James not playing: “Bryce and I had a great conversation. I wish I would have got him in the game. It just kind of got tight there and we got the lead. It’s just one of those things, you get the lead, playing a certain way, and then they come back, and then sometimes it’s hard to kind of thrust a guy into that moment when he hasn’t been on the court much. I went with the guys who had been out there and were able to get us that lead, and hoping they could do it again. But Bryce has really shown me a lot the last couple weeks, and we’ll continue to try to find ways to give him opportunities for sure.” On playing in front of a lot of family and friends: “I wasn’t really nervous. Just more excited. I got a lot of family here, a lot of people, probably like 150 people and all. Not nervous or anything. I just wanted to go out here and win.”

item.title: Pep Guardiola, Julian Nagelsmann listed among favorites for USMNT job
item.description: (Photo by Rich Linley - CameraSport via Getty Images) | CameraSport via Getty Images B.J. Callaghan leads the betting at 3/1, followed by former LAFC manager Steve Cherundolo at 4/1. Pep Guardiola comes in third at 5/1, which would be a spectacular appointment if the Manchester City manager fancied taking o n a new challenge. Pellegrino Matarazzo (6/1) and Mikey Varas (10/1) round out the next tier. Things get particularly interesting further down the list. Thierry Henry and Roberto Martinez are both priced a t 14/1, while Julian Nagelsmann comes in at 25/1. Yes, the former Germany head coach is apparently in the conversation. Nagelsmann was dismissed by Germany last summer, so he is technically available, but convincing a coach of hi s pedigree to take on the USMNT project would still be quite the achievement. Perha ps the U.S. Soccer Federation is hoping that a change of scenery and a home World Cup opportunity will be enough to get his attention. It would certainly be an upgrade from simply recycling the usual collection of familiar candidates! Gareth Southgate is also listed at 25/1, follow ed by Didier Deschamps at 30/1. Jesse Marsch (30/1), Eddie Howe (40/1), and Antonio Conte (50/1) complete the list. Of course, betting odds are not confirmation of interest, and some of these names are considerably more realistic than others. Here is the full list per CSB : B.J. Callaghan – 3/1 Steve Cherundolo – 4/1 Pep Guardiola – 5/1 Pellegrino Matarazzo – 6/1 Mikey Varas – 10/1 Thierry Henry – 14/1 Roberto Martinez – 14/1 Julian Nagelsmann – 25/1 Gareth Southgate – 25/1 Didier Deschamps – 30/1 Jesse Marsch – 30/1 Eddie Howe – 40/1 Antonio Conte – 50/1 The United States has home-field advantage at the 2026 World Cup, an increa singly talented player pool, and a genuine opportunity to make a statement on the international stage. The next appointment needs to be s omeone capable of maximizing that potential rather than simply being a recognizable name. Guardiola would be the dream appoi ntment, but there are plenty of intriguing alternatives. Nagelsmann would be a particularly ambitious option, even if his inclu sion on thi s list raises a few eyebrows. Join the conversation! item.title: Magic’s Sean Sweeney gives Jalen Suggs his flowers after returning from injury
item.description: Mike Watters-Imagn Images Magic’s Sean Sweeney gives Jalen Suggs his flowers after returning from injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Orlando Magic notched their first victory at home after beating the Milwaukee Bucks, 107-99 , at Kia Center in the NBA Cup on Friday. The Magic are on a three-game winning streak, improving to 5-7, while the Bucks fell to 1-12. Jalen Suggs returned to action after missing eight games due to a knee injury. He contributed three points, two rebounds, and three assists in 21 minutes off the bench. While he struggled from the field, shooting just 1-of-8, including 1-of-6 from long range, coach Sean Sweeney recognized the overall impact of the sixth-year guard, as reported by Sentinel Sports’ Jason Beede. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “(We) talked a little bit before the game about how, with certain guys when they come back from back injury, they’re trying to manage it, making it a 40-minute game instead of a 48-minute game. But his impact was felt immediately,” said Sweeney. “Although he didn’t have a great shooting night, he impacts the game in so many different areas: On the basketball with his point-of-attack defense, his ability to penetrate and make the right play. In limited minutes, he had three assists, and he had a number of potential assists. So, (it was) great to have him back out there and excited for him to keep ramping up.” #Magic coach Sean Sweeney said they were just trying to manage the game for Jalen Suggs when I asked what went into him coming off the bench in his first game back from injury. “But his impact was felt immediately and … he impacts the game in so many different areas…” More: pic.twitter.com/lR2tyQY310 — Jason Beede (@therealBeede) November 14, 2026 The 25-year-old Suggs has struggled to stay healthy. He has played at least 60 games only once since the Magic drafted him with the No. 5 pick in 2021. When he is on the floor, he gives Orlando a two-way weapon with his energy and doggedness. While Anthony Black has filled in well, the Magic are better with Suggs in the lineup. Suggs and the Magic will have a two-day break before hosting the Boston Celtics on Monday. Related: Magic’s Franz Wagner extends heater to 4 games in win over Bucks Related: Magic’s Franz Wagner embarrassing Bucks with scorching hot start

item.title: South Fort Myers upsets Naples for first playoff win since 2014
item.description: Having spent a majority of their season on the road, there is little that can unnerve the Wolfpack. Even one of the most difficult venues for away teams in Staver Field and a round of the playoffs where the Golden Eagles have historically succeeded. No. 6 seed South Fort Myers imposed its will on defense and relied on the legs of junior quarterback Jaydon Henderson to knock off the third-seed Naples 32-27 in the Class 4A-Region 3 quarterfinal on Friday, Nov. 13. The teams came in with plenty of familiarity after splitting meetings last year with the Golden Eagles getting the final say with a 21-13 first-round playoff victory. “It feels lovely,” South Fort Myers senior defensive lineman Ja’Dell Carter said. “It’s always good to win at Naples.” Carter and the South defense led the way, holding the Naples rushing attack in check for most of the game and forcing four turnovers. The first came when sophomore Jer’Shard Benjamin leapt up to intercept a pass by junior Naples quarterback Devin Dunford. Benjamin was rewarded immediately as Henderson found him streaking behind the defense for a 67-yard score. “So goes (Benjamin), so goes our team,” South head coach Matt Holderfield said. “He brings so much to us both offensively and defensively and special teams. He’s got to have a big game for us to have a big game.” Benjamin would intercept Dunford again in the first quarter, and the Wolfpack once again took advantage with a big play on a 51-yard touchdown run down the sideline by senior Arthur Gallishaw to go up 13-0. The Naples offense started to get going in the second quarter, and junior running back Jevan Raphael got the team on the board with a 17-yard scamper. The Wolfpack stayed heavy with the run, primarily with Henderson making plays to get the team down the field. He capped a second quarter drive with a 19-yard touchdown after avoiding the Naples rush and scrambling to the house. The Golden Eagles ensured themselves a chance with a 1-yard Raphael touchdown run in the final seconds of the half to cut the South lead to 19-14. The third quarter saw the biggest momentum swing of the night when Naples senior Jelani Georges blocked a South punt. In the ensuing chaos, South junior Jaylen Babb scooped up the ball and returned it to the Naples 1-yard line. Henderson scored to put South up 25-14. “It was huge,” Holderfield said. “That was just hustle by our guys. The thing about it is, this time of year, you’re going to need some things like that to happen.” An 80-yard pick-6 by South junior Damod McGuire put South up by three scores early in the fourth quarter. South would recover an onside kick attempt in the final minutes to secure the program’s first playoff win since the 2014 season. Even one of the most difficult venues for away teams in Staver Field and a round of the playoffs where the Golden Eagles have historically succeeded. No. 6 seed South Fort Myers imposed its will on defense and relied on the legs of junior quarterback Jaydon Henderson to knock off the third-seed Naples 32-27 in the Class 4A-Region 3 quarterfinal on Friday, Nov. 13. Benjamin was rewarded immediately as Henderson found him streaking behind the defense for a 67-yard score. “So goes (Benjamin), so goes our team,” South head coach Matt Holderfield said. “He brings so much to us both offensively and defensively and special teams. He’s got to have a big game for us to have a big game.” Benjamin would intercept Dunford again in the first quarter, and the Wolfpack once again took advantage with a big play on a 51-yard touchdown run down the sideline by senior Arthur Gallishaw to go up 13-0. The Naples offense started to get going in the second quarter, and junior running back Jevan Raphael got the team on the board with a 17-yard scamper. The Wolfpack stayed heavy with the run, primarily with Henderson making plays to get the team down the field. He capped a second quarter drive with a 19-yard touchdown after avoiding the Naples rush and scrambling to the house. The Golden Eagles ensured themselves a chance with a 1-yard Raphael touchdown run in the final seconds of the half to cut the South lead to 19-14. The third quarter saw the biggest momentum swing of the night when Naples senior Jelani Georges blocked a South punt. In the ensuing chaos, South junior Jaylen Babb scooped up the ball and returned it to the Naples 1-yard line. Henderson scored to put South up 25-14. “It was huge,” Holderfield said. “That was just hustle by our guys. The thing about it is, this time of year, you’re going to need some things like that to happen.” An 80-yard pick-6 by South junior Damod McGuire put South up by three scores early in the fourth quarter. The Golden Eagles wouldn’t go down easy as Raphael scored his third and fourth touchdowns from 13 and 26 yards out, but the clock wasn’t a friend of the home team. South would recover an onside kick attempt in the final minutes to secure the program’s first playoff win since the 2014 season. The defense led the charge – even with a pair of three-star prospects on the line in Carter and Cornelius Tims – the team relied on all 11 in uniform to get the job done. Holderfield pointed out that several players, like freshman defensive tackle Kymani Cyrus, were key in filling in for injured players. “We knew (Cornelius Tims) and Ja’Dell would have big games,” Holderfield said. “This is what they’re living for right now, but what I’m really proud of is the other guys. We’ve got really young guys that behind them that are coming in and playing.” On the offensive side, Henderson powered his way to 113 rushing yards and two touchdowns, plus 87 passing yards and a score. For Naples, it’s the team’s first loss in the regional quarterfinal round since the 2004 season. The Golden Eagles blitzed the competition in Class 4A-District 12 to win the title but were handed a tough draw in a South Fort Myers team that wouldn’t be daunted by the stakes. “Coach Holderfield does a really good job of just coaching them up and getting them ready to play, and, when you have a well-coached team and they’re super athletic, it’s really hard to beat them,” Naples head coach Rick Martin said. Raphael rushed for 120 yards and four touchdowns against a tough South front, and senior Nicksen Volvic added 109 yards on the ground. The Golden Eagles finish their season with a 6-5 record. “I’m so proud of these guys,” Martin said. "Whether you look at it from just the season and where we started in the spring game to now, the growth and the maturity of this team has just been amazing to watch.” The Wolfpack will once again hit the road for their eighth away game of the season when they face No. 2 seed Tampa Jesuit, which downed Estero 47-14. “Anytime you come down here and win – we’ve been lucky to win a few down here now, and it’s nice,” Holderfield said. “It’s always special. That’s a good team. They’re always well coached. They’re always well prepared, and it’s Naples. It’s big for us. The biggest thing now we got to do is get that out of our head and get ready to go again. It’s something we haven’t done in a while – having to get ready for another one, so it’ll be a big week for us.” This article originally appeared on Fort Myers News-Press: South Fort Myers upsets Naples for first playoff win since 2014

item.title: Jensen Beach's furious rally falls short in Region 4-4A loss to McArthur
item.description: JENSEN BEACH – Sylvester Brinkley carried the ball from the endzone through the post-game handshake line. The Jensen Beach High senior wide receiver insisted he caught the bomb from Dre Lott that would have brought the Falcons to within a point. “Yes,” Brinkley said emphatically. The referees, who had an active evening, disagreed. Jensen Beach dropped the Class 4A-Region 4 quarterfinal to visiting McArthur High out of Hollywood, 21-14, Friday night at the Bird Cage. Falcons coach Tim Caffey agreed with Brinkley. “He did,” Caffey said. “But you can’t leave things up to … If you take care of your responsibility early, you don’t have to worry about something like that. Let’s put it that way.” Mounting a comeback Sixth-seeded Jensen Beach (8-3) trailed the third-seeded Mustangs, 21-0, midway through the fourth quarter when McArthur (4-7) looked to increase its margin. The Mustangs’ 40-yard field goal attempt was blocked by the middle of the line. Junior defensive back Jai’yis Wesley picked up the loose ball and went 75 yards to paydirt to give the Falcons a pulse. “The next thing you know, they are biting their nails and teeth and going, we need to stop them,” Caffey said. “That’s what you want to do: Give yourself a fighting chance at the end. We did. We just didn’t pull it out.” Jensen Beach’s defense then rose to the occasion again, stopping McArthur on a three-and-out to force a punt. The Falcons took over at their own 15-yard line with 5 minutes, 18 seconds remaining in regulation. Caffey disregarded the plays that he thought would work coming into the game and went with what he thought would work after watching the Mustangs’ defense. The Falcons went on their best drive of the game. Lott hit nine straight passes and went 11-for-14 in the march. On a fourth-and-goal situation from 7 yards out, the junior quarterback took it in for a touchdown. Damion Heissenberg’s PAT kick made it a 21-14 game with 14 seconds left. “It was our best drive of the game,” Caffey said. “There were some things we needed to do. We had to get away from the play-call sheet and go by what we saw. And sometimes you have to do that, make the adjustment.” Things really became interesting when senior linebacker Cason Sweeney recovered the onside kick for Jensen Beach. Starting at its own 49-yard line with 12.1 seconds remaining, Lott hit junior Gage Wilson for a 4-yard gain. Wilson got out of bounds to stop the clock and set up one more play. Lott heaved the ball nearly 60 yards to the end zone where a group of seven players converged. Brinkley claims he came down with the ball that was later knocked away by a McArthur defender ending the Falcons’ frantic and furious comeback. Jensen Beach had a total of 61 yards through the first three quarters before getting 85 on its penultimate possession. “We had too many mistakes,” Caffey said. “We imploded.” Flag night The teams combined for a whopping 40 accepted penalties for a total of 275 yards marked off. Jensen Beach was penalize

Falcons coach Tim Caffey agreed with Brinkley. “He did,” Caffey said. “But you can’t leave things up to … If you take care of your responsibility early, you don’t have to worry about something like that. Let’s put it that way.” Mounting a comeback Sixth-seeded Jensen Beach (8-3) trailed the third-seeded Mustangs, 21-0, midway through the fourth quarter when McArthur (4-7) looked to increase its margin. The Mustangs’ 40-yard field goal attempt was blocked by the middle of the line. Junior defensive back Jai’yis Wesley picked up the loose ball and went 75 yards to paydirt to give the Falcons a pulse. “The next thing you know, they are biting their nails and teeth and going, we need to stop them,” Caffey said. “That’s what you want to do: Give yourself a fighting chance at the end. We did. We just didn’t pull it out.” Jensen Beach’s defense then rose to the occasion again, stopping McArthur on a three-and-out to force a punt. The Falcons took over at their own 15-yard line with 5 minutes, 18 seconds remaining in regulation. Caffey disregarded the plays that he thought would work coming into the game and went with what he thought would work after watching the Mustangs’ defense. The Falcons went on their best drive of the game. Lott hit nine straight passes and went 11-for-14 in the march. On a fourth-and-goal situation from 7 yards out, the junior quarterback took it in for a touchdown. Damion Heissenberg’s PAT kick made it a 21-14 game with 14 seconds left. “It was our best drive of the game,” Caffey said. “There were some things we needed to do. We had to get away from the play-call sheet and go by what we saw. And sometimes you have to do that, make the adjustment.” Things really became interesting when senior linebacker Cason Sweeney recovered the onside kick for Jensen Beach. Starting at its own 49-yard line with 12.1 seconds remaining, Lott hit junior Gage Wilson for a 4-yard gain. Wilson got out of bounds to stop the clock and set up one more play. Lott heaved the ball nearly 60 yards to the end zone where a group of seven players converged. Brinkley claims he came down with the ball that was later knocked away by a McArthur defender ending the Falcons’ frantic and furious comeback. Jensen Beach had a total of 61 yards through the first three quarters before getting 85 on its penultimate possession. “We had too many mistakes,” Caffey said. “We imploded.” Flag night The teams combined for a whopping 40 accepted penalties for a total of 275 yards marked off. Jensen Beach was penalized 21 times for 108 yards; the Mustangs’ 19 times for 167 yards. McArthur’s Jennings Pierre-Saint picked off Lott on a tipped ball on the Falcons’ first possession leading to the opening score. The Mustangs went 69 yards in a penalty-filled drive that ended with Antron Branch’s 1-yard score. Following a pick by senior Jalen Webley midway through the second quarter, the Falcons got down to the McArthur 2. Caffey elected not to kick a field goal, and Tommy Neloms stopped Alex Thornton for a 3-yard loss on fourth-and-goal. “I had a bonehead decision. I probably should have taken the three, not that it would have made a difference later on,” Caffey said. “But I probably should have taken the three. “We were thinking we could score. We had a mistake in understanding in what we needed to do offensively. And when we finally figured it out, we ran out of time.” McArthur, which played the fourth-toughest schedule in the state, got two quick touchdowns in the third quarter to take a 21-0 advantage. Branch had his second score, a run from 5 yards out. Jackson Stroud, who had a touchdown to Ratavion McCreed nullified in the second quarter because of a penalty, hooked up with McCreed for an 80-yarder that counted. “Helluva job by McArthur. They did a heckuva job,” Caffey said. “They hit some long throws on us. That’s pretty much it.” McArthur, which lost to Mandarin, Cardinal Gibbons, Dillard, Norland, St. Thomas Aquinas, Chaminade Madonna and American Heritage-Plantation – teams that went a combined 50-19 – during the regular season, had 57 yards in the first half and 153 for the game, 18 on the ground. “Our defense played its best,” Caffey said. “We had a lack of understanding of what we needed to do in the process. And it was both sides of the ball.” Jensen Beach suffered its first home loss in seven games this season “The wins are on the kids; the losses are on me,” Caffey said 17 Falcons graduate Jensen Beach lists 17 seniors on its roster. “It was tough,” Caffey said. “I hated it for some of our seniors, like Alex Thornton and Sylvester Brinkley, kids who have been with me. It’s emotional, man.” Those seniors have gone to the postseason all four years and won three district championships and county championships. “So they’ve done a helluva job,” Caffey said. “I hate for them to lose this way. But it’s typical Jensen Beach. They are going to fight to the end. They are giving us a fighting chance at the end to think we can pull it out. It didn’t happen and we have to move on. “But here’s what I’ll tell ya, those kids over there are going to give you everything they’ve got. And that’s going to go way, way deep in life with that, knowing that I can battle no matter what the circumstances are.” This article originally appeared on Treasure Coast Newspapers: Jensen Beach's furious rally falls short in Region 4-4A loss to McArthur

item.title: Fair Grove turns whiteboard motivation into district championship reality
item.description: SPRINGFIELD — Josh Evans always writes three things on his whiteboard. The first-year Fair Grove head coach emphasizes three things that will lead the team to victory. The Eagles met all three of his goals on Friday, Nov. 13. Fair Grove defeated Springfield Catholic 47-7 to win the district championship. “I love seeing these guys have success,” Evans said. “I’ve been really hard on these guys, so to see them be successful gets me juiced up, genuinely.” On the whiteboard, Evans wrote with a marker that his team must move their feet on contact, allow no big moments and force with violence. “If we play every rep like it is a big moment, then there is truly no big moment,” Evans said. “Forcing the ball back in with violence, not skipping past. Being violent at the point of the attack." Watch: Fair Grove douse head coach Josh Evans with Gatorade bath Those three commands weren’t just written on a board in the locker room. They were lived on the field for all to see in a high-stakes playoff game. Fair Grove opened the scoring through a rushing touchdown from Austin Azeez. Springfield Catholic would respond with a long rushing touchdown from Sam Boston. The two teams are deadlocked 7-7 at the end of the first quarter. For the final three quarters, everything went Fair Grove’s way. The Eagles forced four turnovers and stopped the Irish on a 4th-and-inches around midfield. Fair Grove’s Gavin Strong was all over the field, including two interceptions. Fair Grove quarterback Gavin Thomason was electric behind a fantastic offensive line performance. He scored four touchdowns, featuring short, physical runs and long, lung-bursting scores. “We’ve been wanting this game all year,” Thomason said. “They couldn’t stop it, so we just kept running it down their throats.” Republic: 'Greek God' Baelor Cutbirth emerging as a top talent Along with Thomason, running back Wyatt Hallam totted the rock efficiently. He also added two touchdowns. The dynamic duo was not going to let what happened earlier in the season happen again. Springfield Catholic took down Fair Grove 27-22 on Sept. 25. Since then, Fair Grove has had this game circled on their schedule. The Eagles have been relentless since their only defeat, outscoring opponents 341-48 in the previous seven games. “Ever since that game, we’ve been running our butts off in practice,” Hallam said. “We made it happen this time.” After every win, Fair Grove has celebrated to one specific song. “I don’t know what it is,” Evans laughed. “I’m getting too old for this.” “It’s called ‘La Mama de la Mama,’” Hallam said. “It’s a Spanish song, so when it comes on, we get pretty hyped in the locker room.” Fair Grove hopes to keep dancing and singing together over the next few weeks. The Eagles have another stern test in the Class 2 State Quarterfinals. He scored four touchdowns, featuring short, physical runs and long, lung-bursting scores. “We’ve been wanting this game all year,” Thomason said. “They couldn’t stop it, so we just kept running it down their throats.” Republic: 'Greek God' Baelor Cutbirth emerging as a top talent Along with Thomason, running back Wyatt Hallam totted the rock efficiently. He also added two touchdowns. The dynamic duo was not going to let what happened earlier in the season happen again. Springfield Catholic took down Fair Grove 27-22 on Sept. 25. Since then, Fair Grove has had this game circled on their schedule. The Eagles have been relentless since their only defeat, outscoring opponents 341-48 in the previous seven games. “Ever since that game, we’ve been running our butts off in practice,” Hallam said. “We made it happen this time.” After every win, Fair Grove has celebrated to one specific song. “I don’t know what it is,” Evans laughed. “I’m getting too old for this.” “It’s called ‘La Mama de la Mama,’” Hallam said. “It’s a Spanish song, so when it comes on, we get pretty hyped in the locker room.” Fair Grove hopes to keep dancing and singing together over the next few weeks. The Eagles have another stern test in the Class 2 State Quarterfinals. This is Fair Grove’s first state quarterfinal since 2024. “We’ve been preaching to everyone what it takes and what it means to get there,” Thomason said. “It really starts with our scout team.” The Eagles will host Lamar (11-0) at 1 p.m. on Saturday, Nov. 21. Liam Keating covers high school sports and Missouri State athletics for The Springfield News-Leader. Send stats or information to him at Lkeating@usatodayco.com This article originally appeared on Springfield News-Leader: Fair Grove turns whiteboard motivation into district championship reality

item.title: The Anti-Preview: No. 3 Notre Dame Fighting Irish VS Boston College Eagles
item.description: We made it. The Notre Dame Fighting Irish are very much alive in the race for the college football playoff. That race was very much in the air last week when the Irish hosted Miami, but Notre Dame passed the test — and now it’s on to a different kind of test over these next three games. The first of the final trilogy is an old foe who has stuck a knife into Notre Dame and twisted it a number of times, the Boston College Eagles. Boston College is a bad football team. WHAT SHOULD YOU BE EATING? Dunkin It’s late, and you got things to do. Just grab some Dunkin Donuts. WHAT SHOULD YOU BE DRINKING? I mean… there’s only one drink that goes with donuts (other than coffee) and that’s the ancient honey liqueur that is Irish Mist. Irish Mist THREE OTHER GAMES It’s not the so-called “separation Saturday” but there are a lot of interesting games this week, and a large amount of them have direct impact on the CFP. Here are the three games you should pay the closest attention to on Saturday (or whenever they can play). Wake Forest Demon Deacons VS SMU Mustangs — NOON Michigan Wolverines VS Oregon Ducks — 3:30 PM Arizona Wildcats VS Utah Utes — 10:30 PM I’m not sure that SMU will have a number next to its name if they beat Wake Forest and travel to Notre Dame, but it would be nice. Michigan and Oregon are playing to make this a TERRIBLE season for both, and I’m here for that. Maybe the biggest one for Notre Dame to watch is out west with Arizona and Utah… like is this game for real? THE POD BABY PREDICTION I keep saying that this game will either look like the Stanford game from this year, or the Boston College game from last year. Notre Dame is going to win, but how — and how good does it look. I’m not worried about rankings or the committee, but I do want to know how the Irish handle a little success. I choose the blowout. Notre Dame does a better job this week of getting ready for its opponent rather than extending the Miami celebration. CJ Carr has a Heisman to win, and the offense gets lethal. Notre Dame 48, Boston College 6

item.title: Warriors find there's no replacement for Steph Curry, as 38-point loss in San Antonio shows
item.description: Golden State Warriors guard Brandin Podziemski passes as he is guarded by San Antonio Spurs forward Julian Champagnie, second from left, during the first half Friday. (Darren Abate/Associated Press) SAN ANTONIO - Two nights earlier, Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg sat on a bench in Houston and closed his eyes as a new world unfurled beyond the blackness. His NBA existence, for 12 games, had been devoted to supporting teammate Stephen Curry . But Curry had winced, and grimaced, and grabbed at a torn oblique, and walked off the floor to an indefinite absence. Lendeborg is who remained. Warriors teammates, late in the first quarter against the Rockets, told Lendeborg he needed to step up. They knew he could. They'd seen it. So Lendeborg meditated for a moment, there at the Toyota Center, and tried to tell himself he could. I gotta do this, he recalled thinking, later. I am able to do this. I am good enough. "Just positive self-talk," Lendeborg said Friday morning, hours before a 123-85 loss to the Spurs in San Antonio. "That usually helps me out." "And if it doesn't," the 24-year-old continued, with full transparency, "I'm kinda gonna be f-ed the rest of the game." It helped in Houston. It didn't help in San Antonio, this night. His own anticipated outcome did, in fact, occur. Hope up and flew away, the second Curry's soles left the tarmac in San Antonio and boarded an early jet back to the Bay Area. He is set for at least a couple weeks of rehabilitation with Warriors director of performance Rick Celebrini, trying to heal a torn oblique with expedited caution. And Golden State - with Lendeborg and 23-year-old Brandin Podziemski trying to lead the charge - looked like a team whose season had frozen in time without him. So Lendeborg meditated for a moment, there at the Toyota Center, and tried to tell himself he could. I gotta do this, he recalled thinking, later. I am able to do this. I am good enough. He is set for at least a couple weeks of rehabilitation with Warriors director of performance Rick Celebrini, trying to heal a torn oblique with expedited caution. And Golden State - with Lendeborg and 23-year-old Brandin Podziemski trying to lead the charge - looked like a team whose season had frozen in time without him. Team Rebounds: 8. Team Turnovers: 2. Blocked Shots: 7 (Kornet 2, Wembanyama 2, Castle, Champagnie, McLaughlin). Turnovers: 9 (Fox 2, Johnson 2, Wembanyama 2, Barnes, Castle, Champagnie). Steals: 7 (Reed Jr. 2, Fox, Harper, Johnson, McLaughlin, Wembanyama). Technical Fouls: None. Golden State 14 19 27 25 - 85 San Antonio 38 25 34 26 - 123 A: 18,849 (18,581). They looked like a team, actually, that had completely forgotten how to play basketball. In a literally unprecedented development in franchise history, the Warriors were blitzed 18-0 to start by San Antonio, the most unanswered points surrendered by Golden State to start a game since the play-by-play tracking era began in 1997-98. It didn't help they walked into an ambush at the Frost Bank Center, against a young Spurs team that operates like an organized pack of sharks with katanas strapped to their dorsal fins. Ascending face-of-the-NBA Victor Wembanyama played 15 first-half minutes; the Warriors tallied a total of 14 points in the first quarter. "Wemby's like 7-foot-10?" Lendeborg questioned pregame, half-joking, when asked the tallest player he's ever faced. It's 7-foot-4, actually. But he might as well have been. Every single Warrior who stepped on the floor during Wembanyama's minutes - save for a silver-line-weaving LJ Cryer, who dropped a career-high 20 points - looked utterly uninterested in attacking the rim. In the third quarter, Warriors forward Gui Santos turned the corner on an open lane, saw Wembanyama lurking in the paint, suddenly picked up his dribble and found the nearest open Warrior, and De'Anthony Melton air-balled a three. Copy-paste that sequence, for most of the night. A year ago, Curry walked into San Antonio and dropped 46 and 49 points in two wins across three nights, his individual brilliance enough to lift the Warriors over a deeper and fresher and quicker team. Without him, the Warriors' system visibly imploded. Second-year catch-and-shoot wing Will Richard curled off a dribble handoff for a strange elbow jumper, and Melton and Cryer fired up a few in-between floaters with no better option, and Draymond Green looked lost offensively without his pick-and-roll mate, eventually charging in to knock over Wembanyama for a second-quarter flagrant foul that appeared to carry little purpose. This was a remarkably unfavorable draw, in the first game of a Curry absence that could reasonably stretch a ways into December. Chalk it up to the Wemby Effect, sure. But glaring alarm bells emerged with Lendeborg's ability to adjust to a mental reality as Golden State's No. 1 option - and adjust to defenses treating him as such. After 12 games of head-hunting defenders and letting step-back threes fly without much hesitation, Lendeborg looked hesitant to find his own shot in the first half with San Antonio often sending multiple bodies in his direction. In the second half, when trying to generate offense, he looked completely out of sync, finishing 1-for-13 for three points and three turnovers in a -40 stint in 23 minutes of game action. "Probably six out of 10," Lendeborg said at shootaround, asked his comfort level with stepping in as Golden State's No. 1 option. "It's like - it'll be fun. Just trying to figure out what ways I can score best, or what I gotta do to be able to be an efficient scorer. And then the other four is like, ‘Man, am I going to be able to live up to it and be able to help out the team the way I want to?' But, you know, time will tell." Time offered a sharp reality check on Friday. And in an equally pressing issue, Podziemski looked utterly out of whack from tip-off, unable to generate much chemistry in replacing Curry in two-man action with Green and frequently picking up his dribble without a decisive move to the rim. Podziemski finished 2-for-10, and no other Warriors starter could generate a lick of offense. Golden State took 10 shots between the restricted area and the 3-point line in the first quarter (and went 0-for-10), and attempted just two shots at the rim. The starters went 4-for-27 from the floor in the first half. And a joyous early eight-game win streak, persisting and prevailing just a handful of days ago, felt like a distant memory in San Antonio. item.title: Pueblo East defeats Severance on last-second field goal in football playoffs
item.description: The Pueblo East Eagles hosted the Severance Silver Knights on Friday, Nov. 13, at Dutch Clark Stadium in the second round of the CHSAA Class 3A football playoffs. East and Severance battled it out on a cold night on the gridiron. It was mostly a defensive battle all night long with both teams forcing several turnovers in the game and multiple punts. Severance got on the board first in the first quarter with a Max Yahn touchdown. East answered back in the second quarter with a passing touchdown from Dion Alsworth to Brayden Diaz to tie the game 7-7. It would remain the same score until halftime. In the third quarter, both teams exchanged drives and turnovers and were locked into a big defensive standoff. Neither team could really move the ball down the field. The score stayed the same until late in the fourth quarter, when the Eagles mounted a drive. They went down the field with less than three minutes left on the clock to get into the red zone. More: Live updates: Pueblo area high school football playoffs scoreboard On 4th and 15, Eagles kicker Dylan Cooper stepped up and drilled about a 35-yard field goal to put East up 10-7. Severance, with less than a minute left on the clock could not convert on 4th and long and the Eagles would come away with a 10-7 victory. Eagles head coach Tony Valdez was ecstatic after the game, saying, “We needed this one.” This was Valdez’s first playoff victory as the head coach of the Eagles, and the program's first playoff win in nine years. Valdez spoke after the game about what a fight it was for the Eagles to pull this one off. More: VOTE for the Pueblo Chieftain Football Player of the Year | Round 1 “It's a testament to this team and this program in the last few years,” Valdez said. “We might get down, but we're not out. These guys stick together. They're resilient. They're a true family, and they will never quit on each other. And we won't quit 'til the fat lady sings.” He also talked about what it was like during that final offensive drive that won the game for the Eagles. “Honestly, we got down there, we wanted to get six naturally, and then we got kind of down behind the chain. So it's like, don't make a mistake,” Valdez said. “We got a high-quality All-State field goal kicker, and we trust him with the game on the line. He knocked that sucker home.” With the team ready to set out on the road to face a tough Palisades team, Valdez in the Eagles are ready to take on the challenge. “Love is the strongest emotion. If we continue to love each other, love this game, love our program and community, we will continue to win ball games,” Valdez said. Pueblo East will be on the road next Friday, Nov. 20, at Palisade High School. In other local events, Pueblo West defeated Lutheran 38-35 to advance to the quarterfinals, where they will face off against the winner of Montrose and Air Academy. Pueblo County dropped a heartbreaker to Conifer 28-27 as the Hornets went for a 2-point conversion at the end of the game to win

item.title: BYU’s clash with Baylor moved back after travel troubles
item.description: Aaron Baker-Imagn Images BYU’s clash with Baylor moved back after travel troubles appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baylor Bears are set to make their first trip to Provo to take on BYU football since 2022. However, their highly anticipated road matchup against the Cougars has been delayed due to travel complications caused by the nationwide Federal Aviation Administration ground stop. ESPN’s Pete Thamel reported that Baylor and BYU will now get underway at 7 p.m. ET on Saturday at LaVell Edwards Stadium in Provo. “Baylor’s game at BYU has been rescheduled to 7 p.m. Eastern Time, per a source,” Thamel reported. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The game was originally scheduled for a 3:30 p.m. ET kickoff. However, Baylor’s travel arrangements were thrown into uncertainty after the FAA announced a nationwide ground stop on Friday. According to Deseret News, the Bears had not departed Waco and were forced to remain there while waiting for the travel restrictions to be lifted. Baylor is now expected to travel to Provo early Saturday morning. Moreover, Thamel shared another complication surrounding Baylor’s travel arrangements, explaining why rescheduling the game for Sunday was not a viable option . “One complication for Baylor as they attempt to travel to BYU. BYU can’t play on Sunday because of religious restrictions. So there’s a tight timeline with Baylor unable to leave tonight,” Thamel wrote. The FAA’s decision also affected several other college football programs preparing for their Week 11 road matchups. The nationwide ground stop was announced Friday afternoon due to safety concerns, which created travel disruptions for teams across the country. The restriction was lifted later that night. However, several programs still had to adjust their travel plans ahead of Saturday’s games. For BYU, playing at LaVell Edwards Stadium provides a home-field advantage. However, the delayed kickoff will also require the Cougars to make adjustments to their original game-day preparations. BYU will enter the matchup against Baylor with a 7-2 overall record and a 4-2 mark in Big 12 play. Related: Minnesota moves flight to Saturday morning before Penn State showdown Related: Utah clash with Arizona moved back 3 hours after canceling Friday’s flight

item.title: ‘No, I do not’: Yaxel Lendeborg says he actually disagrees with what Draymond Green said about him
item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Yaxel Lendeborg has been one of the surprise packages in the NBA this season. The Golden State Warriors rookie has been in the headlines since day one, and even though some of his antics have made a lot of noise, his performances have trumped that. That is perhaps why Draymond Green sees a massive future for Lendeborg with the Warriors, but the latter doesn’t necessarily see himself that way. Yaxel Lendeborg says he doesn’t feel he is the future face of the Golden State Warriors Everyone has been raving about Lendeborg’s talent and potential this season, including a player who watches him every day – Green. Before anything had really happened in the season, the 36-year-old said about Lendeborg: “The Golden State Warriors have found the next face of the franchise.” Watching the rookie’s performances since has convinced many people that Green’s prediction was right, but Lendeborg doesn’t feel the same way. Why? Because the youngster didn’t even expect to have such a prominent role in his debut season. When asked about Green’s prediction and if he feels he is the future face of the franchise, Lendeborg said on Prime Video: “No, I do not. No. “When I first got drafted, I just expected to be a guy that sits in a corner, waits for a shot, maybe averages like seven points a game. Now, I’ve somewhat become like the second option on offence. “That’s definitely something I never thought would happen in the NBA.” Having said that, Lendeborg has revealed that he is slowly convincing himself that he has what it takes to become a ‘great’. “I would say like 70 per cent right now. Yeah, almost 100 per cent (I believe I can be great). “I just try to continue to let my mind know and just try to ease it a little bit by saying: ‘I belong here.’ I always use ‘you belong’ because, for a long time, I felt like I didn’t belong in the basketball world, especially now in the NBA.” Lendeborg may not have expected to be in the position he is in today, but he fully deserves all the praise he is getting for his performances. The 24-year-old, who is one of the favourites to win the Rookie of the Year award, has the potential to become a superstar – not just for the Warriors but in the entire NBA. Steph Curry is going nowhere for now, but if Lendeborg continues developing at the same rate, we think he will become the face of the Golden State Warriors franchise when their current superstar calls it a day. item.title: This fact will only strengthen Giants legend Buster Posey’s Hall of Fame candidacy
item.description: © Robert Edwards-Imagn Images This fact will only strengthen Giants legend Buster Posey’s Hall of Fame candidacy appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco Giants are yet to be good on the diamond with Buster Posey at the helm as the team’s president of baseball operations. But Posey has built so much goodwill with both the Giants franchise and its fanbase after he spent the entirety of his illustrious career with the team that he has certainly earned the benefit of the doubt as he gains more and more experience in his executive career. Posey will be eligible for the Hall of Fame as a member of the 2027 class. He spent 13 years with the Giants, won three World Series titles with them (2010, 2012, and 2014), and emerged as a legitimate leader that the entire locker room looked up to. The intangible impact he had on the Giants franchise is unmistakable. He was elite behind the dish and called games for pitchers at such a high level that pitchers, like Jake Peavy, credit him for getting the best out of them. In an appearance on MLB Network, Peavy praised Posey for making the game easy for him to the point where he recorded an ERA of 2.17 in 12 appearances after San Francisco acquired him at the trade deadline. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It’s because [Buster Posey] was calling the pitches,” Peavy said. . @JakePeavy_22 on having a 2.17 ERA with the 2014 Giants as a 33-year-old Trade Deadline acquisition: "It's because [Buster Posey] was calling the pitches." https://t.co/hYNvpjqF1D pic.twitter.com/l1NoPU0FVv — MLB Network (@MLBNetwork) November 13, 2026 Prior to the trade, Peavy had a 4.72 ERA on the season in 20 games with the Boston Red Sox. He was already 33 at the time, so some decline was understandable, but he got a new lease in life with the Giants and helped them win their third World Series title in five years. Peavy would only have two seasons left in the big leagues, but for a good stretch, he turned back the clock thanks in large part to his partnership with Posey. Posey does not have the most eye-popping counting stats. He only had 158 home runs and 729 runs batted in for his career, although he did finish with a batting average of .302. But the Giants would not have won big without him, and the impact he had that stats could not account for must not go unnoticed. Related: Giants rumors: What San Francisco wants in free agency this offseason Related: Giants rumors: Logan Webb trade suitors should take a hike

item.title: Haughton football gets multiple TDs from Brandon Craig to slip past Parkway
item.description: HAUGHTON — Two coaches who detest coaching against each other were forced to do so Friday, Nov. 13, and their teams showed out with one of the most memorable games of the 2026 high school football season in Northwest Louisiana. Haughton coach Matthew Sewell, who’s Buccaneers weren’t supposed to defeat Coy Brotherton’s Parkway squad for a second time in a season, managed to squeak out a 47-46 win in the opening round of the LHSAA Non-Select Division I playoffs “Under the Pines,” as they like to say in Haughton (9-3). That happened thanks to another extraordinary effort by the Bucs’ Brandon Craig, who scored for the seventh time with 2:25 remaining to give his team a 47-40 lead with just over 2 minutes remaining. But the Panthers (5-6) stormed down the field with Bryston McCoy blasting through the middle for a 13-yard score with about a minute left. Parkway went for the two-point conversion pass, which McCoy nearly completed to 6-foot-4 receiver Gary Burney II, but Ethan Johnson was able to tip the ball out the back of the end zone. PREDICTIONS: Shreveport-area high school football playoff first round predictions BYRD COACH: Byrd parts ways with football coach Stacy Ballew after 6 seasons That set off a wild celebration on the Haughton sideline because it allows the Bucs move into the second round where they’ll meet Destrehan (9-2), a 34-6 winner over East St. John, on the road. Neither Sewell nor Brotherton spent time talking at the conclusion of the very lengthy, overly officiated contest, exchanging barbs. That’ll happen at some point next week. The two young coaches take family vacations and dinners together, play golf as a pair and talk every day, according to Brotherton. “I’ve known him his whole life and we’ve been best friends for the last 10 years,” Brotherton said. “Matthew is way better at coaching sports than playing, but people probably know that.” Sewell got the upper hand when their teams met midway through the season in a District 1-5A contest. Most folks agree it’s hard to defeat a team you’re evenly matched with twice in a season. Sewell agreed he’d definitely rather be coaching against anyone else in the state than his friend, which he enjoys poking fun at. “He loves arcade basketball,” Sewell said of Brotherton. The Panthers put the finishing touches on a solid season with the loss that came in front of a packed stadium with standing room only. Jimmy Watson covers Louisiana sports for the USA TODAY Network. Email him at jwatson@shreveporttimes.com and follow him on Twitter @JimmyWatson6. This article originally appeared on Shreveport Times: Haughton football gets multiple TDs from Brandon Craig to slip past Parkway

item.title: Champions again: Bolles extends swimming streak at state meet
item.description: Bolles continued its generations-long streak of aquatic dominance, once more locking down the boys and girls team titles at the Florida High School Athletic Association Class 1A finals on Nov. 13 at Florida Aquatic Swimming and Training. Episcopal's Blakely Hammel also added to her historic resume with a fifth individual state title. Continuing a streak like no other in the Sunshine State, Bolles won its 39th consecutive boys team championship and the 36th in succession for the girls. As usual through most of that run, the final result was never in doubt. Even with a younger-than-usual lineup, the Bolles boys collected 535 points to easily surpass the 182 from runner-up King's Academy of West Palm Beach. The Bulldog girls won nearly as decisively, with 465 points to 219 for Montverde Academy. Watch Florida high school sports live on NFHS Network Got a great play? How to submit your high school sports highlights to the Times-Union Stars of the show for the Bolles boys included senior Thi Rai, winner of the 200-yard individual medley (1:46.69) and 100 breaststroke (53.69); junior Noah Walker, winner of the 100 butterfly (48.47) and 100 backstroke (48.27); and Tommy Lussier, on top in the 50 free (20.04). Bolles also swept the boys relays in automatic All-American times with the 200 medley relay (Walker, Rai, Thomas Smith and Lussier in 1:28.15); the 200 free relay (Christon Joseph, Lussier, Charlie Russell and Walker in 1:21.50); and the 400 free relay (Lussier, Camp Hartman, Kealan Tupper and Domenic Sotomayor). Top-three Bolles boys finishers included Ben Goodman (third in diving), Hartman (second in 200 free), Lucas Lieberman (third in 100 free), Chris Nelson (second in 500 free), Russell (third in 200 IM and 100 breast) and Smith (second in 100 back, third in 100 fly). On the girls side, Heidi Stoute took first in the 100 free (49.64) and 200 free (1:47.07), while Gianna Vasto repeated in diving with 423.15 points and Juliana Costantini won the 100 breast in 1:03.58. The Bolles girls relays also blasted away the pack. The 200 medley relay (Ali Canada, Grace Higdon, Sarah Blaum and Decker Stedman) won in 1:42.45; the 200 free relay (Stoute, Allison Kelly, Stedman and Canada) finished first in 1:32.97; and the 400 free relay (Stedman, Stoute, Blaum and Kelly) swam 3:24.44 for a winning margin of more than seven seconds. Bolles had top-three girls individual finishes from Canada (third in 100 back), Costantini (second in 200 IM), Higdon (third in 100 breast), Kelly (second in 200 and 500 free) and Stedman (third in 200 IM). For Episcopal, Hammel brought home yet another trophy with her first-place in the girls 500 free, swimming 4:48.65. The Florida-committed senior also took third in the 50 free. In addition, Episcopal's Finn Zubero took second in the boys 100 free as the Eagles placed top-15 in both boys and girls overall standings. This article originally appeared on Florida Times-Union: Champions again: Bolles extends swimming streak at state

item.title: New Zealand vs. India 5th ODI prediction, lineups and Bay Oval pitch report — who will win?
item.description: New Zealand vs. India 5th ODI prediction, lineups and Bay Oval pitch report — who will win? originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Matt Henry spent one over turning a cricket match into a demolition site and the rest of this series now has to live in its shadow. Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer were all gone for nought, India were bowled out for 89 in 26.4 overs, and a 244-run defeat at Bay Oval came within a single run of being the heaviest in their ODI history. Yet! India are 2 and New Zealand 1, and Sunday’s finale at Mount Maunganui have a REAL WEIGHT behind it. India have not won a bilateral ODI series away from home since Gautam Gambhir took charge, losing in Sri Lanka, Australia and England. New Zealand, whose run of 11 home series wins has already ended, are trying to avoid a first home series defeat in seven years. New Zealand will be without Henry and Kyle Jamieson, who are now off to the Test camp. Kohli and Rohit are unlikely to play international cricket in New Zealand again, and a full house will expect a fitting farewell. New Zealand vs. India prediction: Who will win? New Zealand will be dearly miss the services of Matt Henry and Kyle Jamieson in this game. Will Young’s 125 and Tim Seifert’s maiden ODI fifty were bright spots, but New Zealand’s batters have not yet found a way to build an innings against this attack. India will be rattled, and Gambhir has admitted he is concerned by their frequent ODI collapses. item.content:encoded: New Zealand vs. India 5th ODI prediction, lineups and Bay Oval pitch report — who will win? originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Matt Henry spent one over turning a cricket match into a demolition site and the rest of this series now has to live in its shadow. Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer were all gone for nought, India were bowled out for 89 in 26.4 overs, and a 244-run defeat at Bay Oval came within a single run of being the heaviest in their ODI history. Yet! India are 2 and New Zealand 1, and Sunday’s finale at Mount Maunganui have a REAL WEIGHT behind it. India have not won a bilateral ODI series away from home since Gautam Gambhir took charge, losing in Sri Lanka, Australia and England. New Zealand, whose run of 11 home series wins has already ended, are trying to avoid a first home series defeat in seven years. New Zealand will be without Henry and Kyle Jamieson, who are now off to the Test camp. Kohli and Rohit are unlikely to play international cricket in New Zealand again, and a full house will expect a fitting farewell. New Zealand vs. India prediction: Who will win? New Zealand will be dearly miss the services of Matt Henry and Kyle Jamieson in this game. Will Young’s 125 and Tim Seifert’s maiden ODI fifty were bright spots, but New Zealand’s batters have not yet found a way to build an innings against this attack. India will be rattled, and Gambhir has admitted he is concerned by their frequent ODI collapses. Still, 89 all out looks more like one terrible morning than a trend especially with such an amount of experience in their ranks. Cricket news prediction : India to win New Zealand vs. India predicted lineups, team news for 5th ODI Here’s how we think both sides will line up. On the New Zealand side, Duffy should come in for one of the vacated pace spots. Tickner , if he has recovered from concussion, and the uncapped Randell are competing for the other. India will be without Shubman Gill, Anshul Kamboj , Jasprit Bumrah and Nitish Kumar Reddy , and Gurnoor Brar , the top wicket-taker of the series, misses out after being called up to the Test squad. New Zealand predicted lineup against India Will Young, Tim Seifert (wk), Nick Kelly, Dean Foxcroft or Mitch Hay, Finn Allen, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner (c), Kristian Clarke, Matt Fisher, Jacob Duffy, Brett Randell India predicted lineup against New Zealand Rohit Sharma, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer (c), Ishan Kishan (wk), Naman Dhir, Axar Patel, Auqib Nabi, Mohammed Siraj, Kuldeep Yadav, Arshdeep Singh New Zealand vs. India pitch report, 5th ODI, Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui Bay Oval did serve up two very different pictures of itself. New Zealand piled up 333 on Friday, and India folded for 89 in under 27 overs, so anyone trying to read the surface has been handed contradictory evidence. The likeliest truth is that it rewards disciplined bowling with a fresh ball and rewards batters who are willing to wait for it to settle. Chasing sides have a small edge in the record, with 17 wins for bowling first against 16 for batting first from 33 matches. Even so, the Friday defence was a rare result under lights at this ground in recent times. The forecast looks kind, so the captain who wins the toss will be choosing on conditions alone and not on any rain calculation. A first innings around the 238 average would be a sound base. item.title: Bloomington South football storms Castle in 2nd half to make history
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, Ind. — Making history is a tough thing to do in a football program as storied as Bloomington South's . But this senior class did it in a big way, winning a fourth straight regional title for the first time ever, using a dominating second half to put away Castle, 38-14 in a Class 5A contest at Huff Memorial Field on Friday, Nov. 13. "It means absolutely everything," South senior linebacker TJ Wilson said. "We've worked our butts off during practice every week. We've been keeping at it. Teamwork is the biggest thing to me. We've just been doing great and it paid off." It moves the Panthers (10-2) on to a road trip to Arsenal Tech in Indianapolis next week to face off with another storied powerhouse, Cathedral (9-3), which pounded Plainfield 45-14, similarly outscoring the Quakers 28-0 in the second half. They've played a lot of football during that streak. I don't know what next week brings, but we're going to fight like hell to try to get to that next step. We just asked for the opportunity and we got it."
