But this senior class did it in a big way, winning a fourth straight regional title for the first time ever, using a dominating second half to put away Castle, 38-14 in a Class 5A contest at Huff Memorial Field on Friday, Nov. 13. "It means absolutely everything," South senior linebacker TJ Wilson said. "We've worked our butts off during practice every week. We've been keeping at it. Teamwork is the biggest thing to me. We've just been doing great and it paid off." It moves the Panthers (10-2) on to a road trip to Arsenal Tech in Indianapolis next week to face off with another storied powerhouse, Cathedral (9-3), which pounded Plainfield 45-14, similarly outscoring the Quakers 28-0 in the second half. More: Bloomington South girls basketball win over North completes county sweep "It's awesome," South coach Gabe Johnson said of the streak. "It's not easy. There's so many people and a lot of them are on the field right now, who had a part in it. And you just want them to enjoy it. "But this senior class has been a huge part of it. They've played a lot of football during that streak. I don't know what next week brings, but we're going to fight like hell to try to get to that next step. We just asked for the opportunity and we got it." Add it up, and that's nine extra games (and nine extra weeks of practice), essentially an extra season's worth, these seniors have helped earn the past three years beyond the 10 allotted each year by the IHSAA. South has won three regionals in a row a few times. But never four. "Going into the week, (Johnson) brought it up," quarterback Duncan Combs said. "But the main goal was to just focus on this game and see how it came out. "We've put in a lot of work over the past three years. It's worked out for us in the tournament. We're playing our best football always when it hits November and that's a great thing." It was a great moment for senior receiver Mayson Lewis to take in after his huge night with five catches for 128 yards and two second-half scores. He had a different perspective coming in just this year after moving over from Terre Haute South. "I'm ecstatic," Lewis said. "I have no words. I come from a program that doesn't win a lot and to come here and win a sectional and a regional championship, it feels amazing. "It's a brotherhood over here. I have all my brothers who pick me up when I'm down. I came here, they were very welcoming. It was great." Combs on target again Combs made some personal history as well, having started for the last three title winners. He was sterling all night, going 18-of-23 for 290 yards and three touchdowns passing and added a wrinkle to the South run game to take some heat off Hayden Clark (22 carries, 92 yards), including a pair of TD runs in the first half. "We're going to take what they give us and they gave us that," Johnson said of the passing game's success. "You saw Duncan run a little more and passes to Ogden a little more. Things you don't see from us a lot and I thought we schemed them well." He is now No. 2 all-time for the Panthers with 6,510 yards passing, second only to Rex Grossman (7,518). His 462 completions are also No. 2 behind Gavin Yeskie (487). The senior also led an important scoring drive right before half after Castle went up 14-10 at 4:41, moving the Panthers 70 yards to score with 23 seconds left on his 3 yard keeper. "That was huge for our mental state to go up," Johnson said. "It felt a little bit like we were down, so I had to remind them we were up." He went on to go 10-of-11 for 171 yards in the second half, hitting junior tight end Derek Ogden five times for 46 yards. Jonathan Winstead caught three balls for 70 yards and Clark was a threat out of the backfield catching three passes. "Ogden, it's his first game with really getting the ball a lot," Combs said. "He's great with finding a way to act like he's blocking and then release into the flat where nobody's looking at him. "Mayson, once he gets the ball, he's gone. You just got to give him a chance." All the same, South never abandoned the run and it paid off with 120 of its 171 ground yards coming in the second half. "Physically, I think we wore on them a little bit," Johnson said. Second-half knock-out punch South's defense was the equivalent of the communications snafu that grounded flights all over the country on Friday. After giving up 145 yards by halftime, the Panthers allowed just 34 more while pitching a second-half shutout. A 2,000-yard passer was held to 109 and a receiver with nearly 800 yards had just two catches for 16 yards. "Castle, great job in the first half," Johnson said. "They came out and kept us off balance. (Head coach Doug Hurt) had a great gameplan. They've got some playmakers out there. "They reminded us of the 2022 team we played and got our butts beat. They kept you off-balance with screens and the run game. They reminded me of that so I was worried about that. We just had to come out and tackle it and stay on it. We made some good halftime adjustments on both sides of the ball." Castle came out throwing more than expected, but it also says something about South's defense that it can absorb the halftime adjustments so well. "We went over plays in the locker room and figured out what we needed to do and we did it," Wilson said. "We're very versatile and whenever we pinpoint something we've made a mistake on, we fix it just like that, in a snap." Meanwhile, the offense got in full gear and once it got going downhill, it was over. "Big credit to the defense," Combs said. "They went in there at halftime, made some adjustments and that got the ball rolling where we could take shots down the field and we were running for six yards a carry it felt like." The Panthers' second possession of the third quarter finished with an 8-yard TD strike to Jonathan Winstead and a 24-14 lead at the 5:11 mark. Castle went on a quick three-and-out for a second straight time and South drove 70 yards, Lewis polishing off the last 22 yards to make it 31-14 with 1:46 left in the period. The Knights' only first down came on a pass interference penalty before they had to punt again. South struck even more quickly this time, as Lewis took a pass on a crossing route and turned on the jets to split two defenders and score from 62 yards out with 9:18 left. "The feeling of us getting a stop and we're all hyped," Wilson said. "And when we go on the sideline and we cheer on our boys and they get in the end zone, it's one of the best feelings you could ever have." item.title: Spurs’ Stephon Castle sets new season high in NBA Cup win over Warriors
item.description: Nov 7, 2026; Portland, Oregon, USA; San Antonio Spurs guard Stephon Castle (5) warms up before a game against the Mandatory Credit: Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images Spurs’ Stephon Castle sets new season high in NBA Cup win over Warriors appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Antonio Spurs made a loud statement in NBA Cup play on Friday night , and Stephon Castle was right at the center of it. The third-year guard poured in a season-high 32 points to lead the Spurs to a 123-85 rout of the Golden State Warriors at Frost Bank Center. Castle was nearly perfect from start to finish. He shot 12-of-18 from the field, including 5-of-8 from beyond the arc, and went 3-of-3 from the free-throw line. He also added six assists and five rebounds, finishing with a game-best plus-35 rating. The performance easily topped his previous season high of 24 points, which he set in the season opener against the Oklahoma City Thunder. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Spurs wasted no time taking control. San Antonio opened the game on an 18-0 run, its largest to start a game in the play-by-play era, and built a 38-14 lead after the first quarter. By halftime, the lead had ballooned to 30, with Castle already sitting on 18 points and four triples. He also found Wembanyama for a lob that the big man finished with a reverse slam . The 2026 NBA Defensive Player of the Year did a bit of everything , posting 12 points, 12 rebounds and six assists. Keldon Johnson chipped in 18 points off the bench, while Harrison Barnes added 11. The Warriors, meanwhile, were shorthanded without Stephen Curry, who is sidelined with a torn oblique . Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody were also out. Golden State shot just 33.3% from the field, with rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who entered averaging 21.7 points per game, going 1-of-13 for three points. LJ Cryer led the way with 20 points on six 3-pointers. With the victory, San Antonio stretched its winning streak to 11 games and improved to 11-2 on the season. The win also gave San Antonio a leg up in the NBA Cup’s Western Conference race, while Golden State dropped to 8-5 overall. The Spurs will look to keep the streak alive when they visit the Utah Jazz on Sunday. Related: Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama wasn’t surprised by push by Draymond Green Related: Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama shows off insane skill set vs. Warriors in NBA Cup

item.title: Cheshire football pulls away from Guilford with late defensive takeaways
item.description: Cheshire linebacker Will Wable helped spark the Rams' 31-6 win over Guilford with a fourth-quarter interception on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, at Cheshire High. (Ron Buck/For Hearst Connecticut Media) CHESHIRE - By playing complementary football , Cheshire unofficially wrapped up a CIAC playoff berth Friday night. The Rams turned two timely fourth-quarter interceptions into touchdowns and scored 14 points in just over a minute late in the game to pull away from Guilford 31-6. Cheshire improved to 7-2 with the win and remained No. 3 in the CIAC Class L playoff standings. The Rams finish the regular season on Thanksgiving morning against Class LL top-seed Southington, which improved to 8-1 with a 38-14 win at Maloney. The neighboring rivals play for a 30th time in the Apple Valley Classic to wrap up the regular season. Guilford is also 7-2 after losing the Southern Connecticut Conference affair, but had already unofficially clinched a Class M postseason spot. The Grizzlies sit No. 5 in playoff points. Nursing a 17-6 halftime lead, the Rams' defense shut out Guilford in the second half. Neither team scored in the third quarter, but the game turned early in the fourth quarter when Will Wable picked off Guilford's Ryan Lynch. The turning point came with Guilford driving. But on fourth down, with 9:36 remaining, Wable stepped into the passing lane at the Cheshire 38 and returned the ball to the Guilford 35. Five plays later, Noel Martinez scored the first of his two touchdowns over the next 1:15 to put Cheshire up 24-6. "I saw (Lynch) roll out but it wouldn't have happened without the defensive line playing great all day," said Wable. "They helped me out a lot, filling the gaps so I could get outside and make a play." On Guilford's next possession, Evan Gonzalez also intercepted Lynch. His interception set up a 28-yard Martinez scamper with 5:44 to play that sealed the Cheshire win. Martinez finished with 142 yards on 18 carries. While the Rams failed to sack Lynch, the sophomore was under pressure all night. Cheshire's bigs up front also kept Guilford running back Shane Connelly in check all night. Connelly came into the game with nearly 1,200 yards (15 TDs) and finished with just 12 yards on 10 carries. The defensive line's play wasn't lost on Gonzalez. "Honestly, the D line is the main part of our defense," Gonzalez said. "When they control the line of scrimmage, that's it. It makes it easy on us on the back end to just flow." The Rams never trailed, taking the opening kickoff 62 yards to a 7-yard touchdown run by junior quarterback Ryan Plouffe. Cheshire made it 14-0 on the first play of the second quarter when Plouffe found Chase Bellair for a 24-yard touchdown pass. "As the game went on, we were able to create some turnovers; and when you win the turnover battle you are going to win a lot of football games," Cheshire head coach Don Drust said. item.title: Raiders’ Future With Maxx Crosby Gets Major Insider Update
item.description: The Las Vegas Raiders continued forward with superstar pass rusher Maxx Crosby on the roster through the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Despite more swirling rumors, Crosby remains with the only franchise he has ever played for since being drafted in 2019. Crosby was traded during the offseason. The Raiders agreed to a trade with the Baltimore Ravens that would have shipped Crosby out of town in exchange for two first-round picks. When all was said and done, the Ravens decided to pull out of the deal. Following that decision from Baltimore, Crosby returned to Las Vegas. Both sides opted to move forward together. While Crosby remains with the Raiders, there are many who don’t expect his reunion to be long-term. There are still trade rumors surrounding him for a reason. He remains a top potential trade candidate to watch heading into the 2027 NFL offseason. Keeping all of that in mind, an NFL insider has offered a new update about Crosby’s future in Las Vegas. Sep 28, 2025; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Las Vegas Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby (98) looks on from the sideline during the first quarter against the Chicago Bears at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Maxx Crosby’s Future With Raiders Gets Major Insider Update According to NFL insider Jason La Canfora, one NFL general manager spoke out and said that he doesn’t think Crosby will finish out his current contract with the Raiders. “He was effectively dealt last March,” La Canfora wrote . “That was a done deal to Baltimore as far as the Raiders were concerned. They aren’t going to get two first-round picks like the Ravens had on the table, but execs think they can get one, plus a day-two pick.” La Canfora continued on, revealing the quote from the general manager. “And with that defense still in deep disrepair, the Raiders are going to need to load up on potential young blue-chip players on that side of the ball. They are still going to be two offseasons away from competing. ‘I don’t think he plays out this contract there,’ one GM told me of Crosby in Vegas .” So far this season in Las Vegas, Crosby has played in nine games. He has recorded 26 total tackles, four sacks, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery, and a defended pass. Throughout his entire 119-game NFL career, he has totaled 465 tackles, 73.5 sacks, 12 forced fumbles, four fumble recoveries, an interception, and 30 defended passes. Kirk Cousins, MIN (@ GB) Kirk Cousins offers another intriguing alternative. He travels to Lambeau Field for an NFC North rivalry game against the Green Bay Packers. Minnesota is coming off a frustrating loss to Buffalo. The matchup against Green Bay, though, could create a different offensive environment. The Packers have an explosive offense of their own, potentially forcing the Vikings to keep pace through the air. Final Takeaway Lock is the top streaming target thanks to his favorable matchup against Las Vegas. Cousins offers passing upside. Smith could benefit from volume. Watson is a deeper-league gamble. Choose according to your roster needs and appetite for risk. item.title: Ime Udoka Addresses Alperen Sengun’s 43-Point Game; Reveals Fred VanVleet Went Off At Rockets’ Bench
item.description: Credits: Imagn Images The Houston Rockets came away with a 125-118 win over the Utah Jazz after a nail-biting matchup that surprisingly went down to the wire despite a dominant performance from Alperen Sengun . He finished with 43 points, 12 rebounds, five assists, one block, and one steal, shooting 17-24 from the field (70.8% FG) and 1-3 from behind the arc (33.3% 3P). This makes him the third player in franchise history (after Hakeem Olajuwon and Yao Ming ) to score 40+ points, grab 10+ rebounds, and dish five assists while shooting 70%+ from the field in a single game. After the win, the Rockets head coach Ime Udoka spoke to the media at the press conference about Alperen Sengun’s big night and also revealed that Fred VanVleet had to shout at the bench to wake them up after the Jazz took a 10-point lead late in the third quarter. “He was dominant. He fouled some guys out. They were blitzing him, and he was finding all the right guys,” Udoka said on Alperen Sengun’s performance. “And he picked them apart so well that they stopped going after him, and he had the matchups that he liked, and we liked. So obviously won the game for us with his scoring. He kind of kept us afloat in the lows and took over towards the end.” After a night with such high usage, Sengun had only one turnover out of the team’s eight. “He was great; they were swarming him a little bit, and he always made the right play. We only had eight (turnovers) as a group, which was phenomenal,” Udoka said. “But for him to handle that much and only have one was a big night and important for us. We had 18 points off of their turnovers, while they only had eight. In a tight game like that, those shots were needed.” This game also highlights the importance of Fred VanVleet on the floor in situations where a young team could have lost its energy after being down by 10 points in a regular-season game. The Jazz were responding to Alperen Sengun’s dominance with their own offensive spurt. But Fred VanVleet provided an essential third-quarter boost that helped the team bounce back. VanVleet finished the game with 17 points, two rebounds, and three assists while shooting 6-11 from the field (54.5% FG) and 3-6 from beyond the arc (50.0% 3P). He scored 10 of his 17 points in the third quarter after apparently shouting at the Rockets’ players, who allowed a 22-point swing in the third quarter that turned a 12-point lead into a 10-point lead for the Jazz. Udoka also spoke about VanVleet’s contributions tonight, including some details on the incident. “He was pissed off with the unit that was in. Kind of went off on everybody, fired himself up, brought the juice and the energy. So we ran him a little bit longer in the third; loved the energy he brought,” Udoka said. “He put the team on his shoulders to create some things off the dribble. So it was needed. We scored 29 in the third quarter, even though we did not defend at all. But a big part of it was him and Alperen being aggressive offensively.” E

item.title: SMU safety Ahmaad Moses is temporarily eligible, expected to play vs. Wake Forest, report says
item.description: SMU safety Ahmaad Moses (3) reacts after breaking up a pass to force a Clemson fourth down during the second quarter of the ACC championship game, Saturday, Dec. 7, 2024, in Charlotte, N.C. (Elías Valverde II/Staff Photographer) SMU safety Ahmaad Moses was temporarily granted eligibility and is expected to make his season debut against No. 13 Wake Forest on Saturday, Billy Embody of On The Pony Express reports . Moses has been fighting for months to be granted a fifth year of eligibility this season, amid a push by athletes in the high school Class of 2022, who have exhausted their eligibility but are pursuing a further chance to play. Moses was granted temporary eligibility in August by a Dallas judge, but he wasn’t medically cleared at the time. By the time he was cleared to play, that order had expired. Last week, a new temporary restraining order request from Moses in Hidalgo County Court was denied. It was not immediately clear which judge granted Moses eligibility ahead of this weekend’s game. The push from athletes in Moses’ class to receive a fifth year comes as the NCAA shifted to a five-for-five eligibility model starting this year. Under the new rule, athletes can play up to five seasons within a five-year window that begins with their initial full-time enrollment in college or the academic year following their 19th birthday — whichever happens first. Athletes in the Class of 2022 say they were the only recent class to miss out on both the new system and the eligibility relief that many athletes in the Classes of 2020 and 2021 received due to the COVID-19 pandemic, prompting their legal action. Moses would’ve gone to the NFL had he not been diagnosed with a herniated disk at the NFL scouting combine , which required spinal fusion surgery. He never signed with a professional team as a result. His addition to SMU ’s roster offers the Mustangs a big boost ahead of a critical conference game. He was a team captain and All-ACC first-team selection in 2025, recording 104 total tackles and a team-high five interceptions. While SMU’s secondary is far improved this season, the Mustangs lost starting safety Tyren Polley Jr . three weeks ago to a season-ending injury. item.title: Global Series Game Two: Hurricanes vs Kraken—Preview, How to Watch, Game Thread
item.description: HELSINKI, FINLAND - NOVEMBER 13: Fans watching as the Seattle Kraken and Carolina Hurricanes practice for the 2026 NHL Global Series Finland at Veikkaus Arena on November 13, 2026 in Helsinki, Finland. (Photo by Brian Babineau/NHLI via Getty Images) *** Local Caption *** | NHLI via Getty Images Admit it, it’s a weird feeling. The calendar year of 2026 is arguably the franchise’s best for the Carolina Hurricanes. We know everything that has happened until now with the playoffs, Cup win, and resulting celebration. It hasn’t stopped since. Seriously, they are at the top of everyone’s power rankings and observers are calling them a wagon. The biggest controversies have been about a player who ultimately came back to them and a jersey that some fans inside and outside the team didn’t like was based on a faux college mascot. On top of all that, they have become the ambassadors for the NHL in this year’s Global Series games in Finland, and they are being treated like fans are lucky to see them—because how many times do the reigning Stanley Cup Champions go abroad? On top of all that, the fans have travelled in high numbers with the team, and on Friday, CNBC revealed their NHL team evaluations and Carolina placed right in the middle ahead of such teams like Colorado, Florida, Minnesota, and Pittsburgh. This is all to say—when you’re watching today’s game in Finland just think about how far this franchise has come in the past decade. A Stanley Cup title game isn’t the time to do so but a neutral ice event where the league chooses teams they feel are marketable to another country is. Judging by the reaction the Canes have gotten in Finland, the right call was made. As for the game itself, there’s more good news on the way. On Friday the Canes had their open practice in front of fans and Finns, and based on the lines it looks like someone may be playing today . It was known that Jordan Staal was on the trip and the hope was he’d play today, and on Friday he skated up with the regulars, centering a line with Jordan Martinook and Seth Jarvis. Afterwards, coach Rod Brind’Amour said that they’ll see how Staal feels today as to whether he’ll play. As the Canes are not doing a morning skate, clearly that decision will be made when everyone wakes up. It might even be known by the time you read this as he’ll have his pregame availability at 10:30 AM Eastern. The thing to note about Staal playing isn’t just that he’s in the lineup, but who’s out. With Staal taking back his line, Mark Jankowski was bumped back to his normal spot. His wingers, though, were Taylor Hall and Jesperi Kotkaniemi. That left Eric Robinson as the odd man out. Also skating with the regulars was Alexander Nikishin back with Shayne Gostisbehere, while Juuso Valimaki was bumped back with extras along with Mike Reilly. Nikishin playing is not a surprise as the Canes want to get him more game action, but it was good that Valimaki got to play one game in front of the home fans. Perhaps the surprise

The calendar year of 2026 is arguably the franchise’s best for the Carolina Hurricanes. We know everything that has happened until now with the playoffs, Cup win, and resulting celebration. It hasn’t stopped since. Seriously, they are at the top of everyone’s power rankings and observers are calling them a wagon. The biggest controversies have been about a player who ultimately came back to them and a jersey that some fans inside and outside the team didn’t like was based on a faux college mascot. On top of all that, they have become the ambassadors for the NHL in this year’s Global Series games in Finland, and they are being treated like fans are lucky to see them—because how many times do the reigning Stanley Cup Champions go abroad? On top of all that, the fans have travelled in high numbers with the team, and on Friday, CNBC revealed their NHL team evaluations and Carolina placed right in the middle ahead of such teams like Colorado, Florida, Minnesota, and Pittsburgh. This is all to say—when you’re watching today’s game in Finland just think about how far this franchise has come in the past decade. A Stanley Cup title game isn’t the time to do so but a neutral ice event where the league chooses teams they feel are marketable to another country is. Judging by the reaction the Canes have gotten in Finland, the right call was made. As for the game itself, there’s more good news on the way. On Friday the Canes had their open practice in front of fans and Finns, and based on the lines it looks like someone may be playing today . It was known that Jordan Staal was on the trip and the hope was he’d play today, and on Friday he skated up with the regulars, centering a line with Jordan Martinook and Seth Jarvis. Afterwards, coach Rod Brind’Amour said that they’ll see how Staal feels today as to whether he’ll play. As the Canes are not doing a morning skate, clearly that decision will be made when everyone wakes up. It might even be known by the time you read this as he’ll have his pregame availability at 10:30 AM Eastern. The thing to note about Staal playing isn’t just that he’s in the lineup, but who’s out. With Staal taking back his line, Mark Jankowski was bumped back to his normal spot. His wingers, though, were Taylor Hall and Jesperi Kotkaniemi. That left Eric Robinson as the odd man out. Also skating with the regulars was Alexander Nikishin back with Shayne Gostisbehere, while Juuso Valimaki was bumped back with extras along with Mike Reilly. Nikishin playing is not a surprise as the Canes want to get him more game action, but it was good that Valimaki got to play one game in front of the home fans. Perhaps the surprise is that Kotkaniemi continues to play, but it really shouldn’t be. This isn’t really about Robinson’s play as it’s about what Kotkaniemi has done since he came back into the lineup. He’s got the same number of goals—five—as Nikolaj Ehlers and Jackson Blake, and he’s more than held his own while having to accept being a healthy extra basically since the mid point of last year. As long as everyone stays healthy he and Robinson will probably switch back and forth as someone to sit in the box, an insane luxury for a team to have. Staal coming back though does bring one problem. Staal’s absence meant that the Canes were able to use his roster spot and keep the likes of Reilly and Valimaki off the waiver wire. Once Staal comes back, though, the Canes will have to send someone down and despite Reilly having a two-way deal, because of his age he would have to clear waivers before going to Chicago. As Valimaki is on a one-way deal and has played more than Reilly, it does seem likely Reilly is the one that’ll be sent down—and then the team holds its breath to see if a defenseman-needy team snaps him up. Between the pipes expect Pyotr Kochetkov to try and knock the rust off after not playing since last Saturday’s mauling of the Blackhawks. If Carolina’s defense is as good in front of Kochetkov as it was in front of Brandon Bussi on Thursday, he shouldn’t have any issues. On the Seattle side, there’s a chance they have a debut coming as well. In their practice it was noted that Jagger Firkus was skating with the regulars on the wing for the first time. He would skate in place of Jani Nyman. The 2022 Second Round pick of the Kraken has been with their AHL team Coachella the last two season and started their this year out of training camp. After the drubbing the Kraken received Thursday there’s little doubt the team felt the injection of “first time energy” would be a good thing. In net, Joey Daccord will be looking to get the win for Seattle. So far this year Daccord has played two less games and has a GAA that’s close to a goal higher than Philipp Grubauer, but their save percentages are close and he brings four wins in with him. He also brings a friendship with the Canes’ Brandon Bussi, as the two caught up over coffee in Finland this week for one of the many wonderful features that have come out with the teams over there. Here’s hoping everyone who made the trip to Finland has had a great time and that the Canes fans will get to celebrate a Finnish Sweep today. If you aren’t there, here’s how you can catch the action: Time: 1 PM Eastern Location: Veikkaus Arena — Helsinki, Finland TV: Hurricanes Hockey Network . Hanna Yates and Shane Willis will handle the pregame duties at 12:30, and then Mike Maniscalco handles play-by-play with Tripp Tracy providing color—You can catch HHN on Spectrum, DirectTV, and Fubo. Note this game will also be nationally broadcast on NHL Network for fans outside of the Hurricanes’ home market. Streaming Video: Hurricanes Hockey Network on Prime Video in the Hurricanes Footprint. Outside the footprint with the game on NHL Network, you will NOT be able to watch the game on ESPN+. Radio: The pregame Storm Watch with Adam Gold on 99.9 The Fan starts at 12:30 PM, At 1 PM radio (consisting of 99.9, 730 The Game in Charlotte, ESPN New Bern 107.5/1490, and ESPN Greenville 107.5/1570) will pick up the Mike Maniscalco and Tripp Tracy TV simulcast. Lines : (Per DraftKings) Hurricanes -375, -1.5 (-148) /Kraken +295, +1.5 (+124). O/U 6.5 +102/-122

item.title: Texas lands in Baton Rouge late Friday after FAA ground stop
item.description: TOPSHOT - Planes wait on the tarmac at Chicago O'Hare International Airport in Chicago, on November 13, 2026. The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has issued a ground stop at all US airports. (Photo by KAMIL KRZACZYNSKI / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images At 2:48 p.m. Central, the social media team for the No. 6 Texas Longhorns posted a video of players boarding the chartered plane heading to Baton Rouge for Saturday’s matchup against the No. 21 LSU Tigers. Bayou bound🤘 pic.twitter.com/gCkcnOkl2e — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 13, 2026 Minutes after the video was posted, the Federal Aviation Administration issued an extraordinarily rare nationwide ground stop for all US airports due to a “temporary telecommunications outage,” only the second ground stop issued by the FAA since September 11, 2001. “Out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted. Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis,” the FAA posted on Twitter. Unable to depart for Baton Rouge, the Longhorns deplaned and headed back to campus in an attempt to maintain the typical Friday routine of a meal, walk-through, and meetings. With the ground stop threatening the team’s ability to make it to Louisiana for the 6:30 p.m. Central kickoff at Tiger Stadium, there was enough pessimism around the 7 p.m. hour for a report to emerge from Chip Brown at Horns247 that the game time could shift to Sunday or Monday. Brown posted his story to Twitter at 7:14 p.m. Central; approximately a minute later, the FAA lifted the ground stop and an official announcement was posted about 15 minutes later. “At 8:15 tonight, Eastern time, we’ve opened up the airspace,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a news briefing. “Now does that mean every flight is going to fly right now? It’s going to be slow. So if you’re watching, you’re at an airport, check with your airline.” As a chartered flight, Texas may have better luck, and Eric Henry’s report from Horns247 indicated that the Longhorns will depart from Austin on Friday night. Duffy publicly encouraged grounded football teams across the country to reach out directly to the FAA to set up flight times to allow Saturday’s games to happen as scheduled. Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin blamed the outage on upgrades patched onto the FAA’s old systems. WOW MULLIN SAYS THE UPGRADES DUFFY PUT IN CAUSED THE OUTAGE “The new technology was overwhelming the older system” pic.twitter.com/GG6oW7CnVF — Acyn (@Acyn) November 14, 2026 Just before 8 p.m. Central, the Horns remained on the Forty Acres and hopeful to leave Austin on Friday with a subsequent upgrade indicating that Texas was expected to arrive in Baton Rouge before midnight after taking off at 10 p.m. Central. *Now* we’re Bayou Bound pic.twitter.com/LXqOgg8sOk — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 14, 2026 The Longhorns landed in Louisiana around 11:30 p.m. Central after a long

item.title: John McGinn double saves Scotland’s blushes against North Macedonia
item.description: A special occasion for Andy Robertson saw Scotland flirt with embarrassment. Collection of his 102nd cap moves him level with Kenny Dalglish in the all-time Scottish list. Robertson will soon be a record holder. This was, however, John McGinn’s night. A double from McGinn, the second a penalty, spared Scottish blushes against a North Macedonia team who threatened to administer red faces to those in navy blue. This proved an almighty struggle for Scotland. Questions – and plenty of them – surround whether or not Sébastien Pocognoli can build on the excellent work of his predecessor Steve Clarke. For now, Scotland are a tough watch. Pocognoli looks tactically inflexible and this is not the new dawn many predicted. Continue reading...

item.title: Jesús Owono given 12-match ban for tackle that resulted in Jesús de Miguel’s death
item.description: FC Andorra goalkeeper collided with De Miguel Owono: ‘I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesús’ The FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono was suspended for 12 matches by the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee on Friday after his challenge on Jesús de Miguel resulted in the death of the Tenerife striker last week. Owono, an Equatorial Guinea international, was sent off in the second division match on 2 November after racing into midfield and colliding with De Miguel while trying to clear an aerial ball. After the collision, De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and the Spanish forward died on 3 November. Continue reading...

item.title: Tuchel to remind England players of anti-racism protocols before game in Spain
item.description: England visit Madrid for first time since fan abuse in 2004 ‘We had the same discussion before the Serbia game’ Thomas Tuchel will remind his ­England players of the anti-racism protocols as they prepare to play Spain in Madrid for the first time since the notorious meeting between the countries in 2004. Spain won 1-0 at the Bernabéu but the occasion was ruined by racist abuse directed at England’s black players from the stands. England have since played three games in Spain, although they refused to return to Madrid for the first of them in 2009. The match was moved to Seville. There were no ­problems in any of the three; the second was in Alicante in 2015, the third back in Seville in 2018. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘No one is unbeatable’: Tuchel eager for England to impose style on Spain
item.description: Manager calls Sunday’s Nations League decider a ‘final’ as preparations for Euro 2028 ratchet up a level Proof of concept. It is Thomas Tuchel’s latest buzz phrase. The England manager has dropped it into the conversation pretty regularly since the Friday of last week when he named his squad for this international window, the one that was always going to decide whether his team finished first or second in their Nations League group. By it, Tuchel means a test of his methods, what he is trying to build – or, more accurately, fine-tune – as he turns his gaze towards Euro 2028 and tries to move on from the devastation of the World Cup semi-final exit against Argentina . The test does not come any bigger than the one which faces him and his players in Madrid on Sunday night. Continue reading...

item.title: Tearful Pochettino says United job was ‘difficult to turn down’ in USMNT farewell
item.description: Coach was ‘transparent’ in dealings with club, federation Pochettino had signed deal to stay with US through 2030 There were always going to be tears at Mauricio Pochettino’s news conference at US Soccer’s national training center on Friday. It was only a matter of when. Pochettino is famously emotional, and nobody in attendance had to wait long for the waterworks – they came during his introductory remarks, as he thanked the US Soccer executives flanking him for the opportunity to guide the US men. He grew emotional again as he addressed his impending departure for Manchester United, one announced just hours earlier. “I think [the decision was],” Pochettino said, pausing to compose himself, “one of the most difficult decisions of our careers. Thank you guys. Thank you so much.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Taking a brief minute to remember Pierre Sage’s impact at Crystal Palace
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! So farewell then, Pierre Sage . Many coaches leave under a cloud, not many have their departures completely obscured by the foul, retch-inducing one emanating from another team’s managerial circus, but such was Sage’s fate . The news section of Crystal Palace’s website helpfully tells you the amount of time it might take you to read each story it links through to. For example it should take four minutes or so to get through Tuesday’s “On this day: five big Crystal Palace birthdays”. “England: I love a knee slide!” will take you five. “Prize draw: be a mascot for our next [Bigger Vase] tie!” is a two-minute job. The statement informing the world of Sage’s exit? One minute. Eighty-three words. By way of illustration, the word “words” was the 84th of this paragraph. Just because the man’s French doesn’t mean his exit should be marked with a shrug. As I have been away at a conference, giving a presentation that the MC described as ‘sobering’, I’ve missed the last few days of football, so I was very sad to read about the passing of the great Danny Kelly . Others are far better placed to give tributes to the great man, but for younger generations who can’t comprehend the football cultural significance, Baker and Kelly represented the peak of football phone-ins. Before it became people ranting and raving about wanting the manager sacked as they’ve lost a few games or wanting the club to spend another few hundred million pounds on yet more players, it was about football supporters and supporting, from fans who actually went to games. Their peak was on BBC Radio in the 1990s, and there are too many examples of their greatness, but if I had to pick one, just one to illustrate it, it would, of course, be Gordon the Dundee United supporter and his bow tie . Rest in Peace, Danny Kelly. You gave us such joy” – Noble Francis. As they no longer seem to be ‘Dr Tottenham’, I was wondering if they had maybe passed the soubriquet on. I think the England cricket team has provided the answer (again)” – Andrew Parker. Impressive list of kiss-off press releases ( yesterday’s Football Daily ) but why was Ralf Rangnick omitted from the chronological list of post-Fergie managers? Is it because Football Daily valued him as little as Manchester United fans did?” – Mike Wilner. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Simon Burnton
item.content:encoded: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! So farewell then, Pierre Sage . Many coaches leave under a cloud, not many have their departures completely obscured by the foul, retch-inducing one emanating from another team’s managerial circus, but such was Sage’s fate . The news section of Crystal Palace’s website helpfully tells you the amount of time it might take you to read each story it links through to. For example it should take four minutes or so to get through Tuesday’s “On this day: five big Crystal Palace birthdays”. “England: I love a knee slide!” will take you five. “Prize draw: be a mascot for our next [Bigger Vase] tie!” is a two-minute job. The statement informing the world of Sage’s exit? One minute. Eighty-three words. By way of illustration, the word “words” was the 84th of this paragraph. Just because the man’s French doesn’t mean his exit should be marked with a shrug. As I have been away at a conference, giving a presentation that the MC described as ‘sobering’, I’ve missed the last few days of football, so I was very sad to read about the passing of the great Danny Kelly . Others are far better placed to give tributes to the great man, but for younger generations who can’t comprehend the football cultural significance, Baker and Kelly represented the peak of football phone-ins. Before it became people ranting and raving about wanting the manager sacked as they’ve lost a few games or wanting the club to spend another few hundred million pounds on yet more players, it was about football supporters and supporting, from fans who actually went to games. Their peak was on BBC Radio in the 1990s, and there are too many examples of their greatness, but if I had to pick one, just one to illustrate it, it would, of course, be Gordon the Dundee United supporter and his bow tie . Rest in Peace, Danny Kelly. You gave us such joy” – Noble Francis. As they no longer seem to be ‘Dr Tottenham’, I was wondering if they had maybe passed the soubriquet on. I think the England cricket team has provided the answer (again)” – Andrew Parker. Impressive list of kiss-off press releases ( yesterday’s Football Daily ) but why was Ralf Rangnick omitted from the chronological list of post-Fergie managers? Is it because Football Daily valued him as little as Manchester United fans did?” – Mike Wilner. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Why Chelsea and Manchester City’s WSL clash is not as season-defining as you think
item.description: Neither side have lost in the league yet but a more competitive division should take title race to the wire There was a time when the games between the top three – traditionally Chelsea, Manchester City and Arsenal – were title-deciders. Where every point taken off a title rival was key. Such was the gap in investment and quality between those teams and the rest of the Women’s Super League, it was extremely rare that points would be dropped to teams outside that elite clique. As the WSL has grown in investment, profile and size, that narrative has started to shift a little. The investment gap is still large from the top to the bottom of the league. But increased investment among the best of the rest and even among those teams further down the table, as well as an increase in high-quality coaches with the tactical and technical vision to get more from players, is having an impact. Continue reading...

item.title: The beautiful game: revived art prize gives football its creative due once more | Emma John
item.description: Football and the art world have long remained distant but the breadth of entries for this year’s award reveals a healthy revival It may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists. The Italian Futurist Umberto Boccioni whirled an athlete’s body into a vortex of movement in his 1913 painting Dynamism of a Soccer Player . You can see one of the earliest fine art depictions of a match – a smoggy, factory-adjactent scene called Any Wintry Afternoon in England – at the Manchester Art Gallery. If 1930s abstraction is more your thing, you can enjoy decoding the geometric shapes in Kazimir Malevich’s Painterly Realism of a Football Player – Color Masses in the 4th Dimension. I’m guessing the small green pea shape is a ball. These, in any case, were exceptions. In 1953 the Football Association launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the FA secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds. Continue reading...

item.description: Argentinian oversaw high-scoring games in his one Chelsea season and Opta predicts his Manchester United side will move upfield quicker than that team Among the 20 managers with more than 290 matches in the Premier League, only the five “ big beasts ” of Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola have better points-per-game averages than Mauricio Pochettino. He is an elite manager. Pochettino took over Southampton midway through their first season back in the top flight (2012-13) after the club spent seven years in the lower leagues. In his only full campaign, they finished eighth. He led Tottenham to second in 2016-17, third in the seasons either side, and reached the 2019 Champions League final . item.title: Michael Carrick was just the latest fall guy for Manchester United’s dysfunctional hierarchy | Jamie Jackson
item.description: Disastrous decisions and confused appointments have been a constant theme at Old Trafford since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013 For a window into the alarming dysfunction at Manchester United that Michael Carrick failed to manage and caused his sacking , consider the case of Eddie Howe, initially a favourite to succeed the 45-year-old before Mauricio Pochettino’s emergence as the chosen one. The former Newcastle manager had been Jason Wilcox’s choice to take over from Carrick. Howe was also the favoured candidate of Dan Ashworth, Wilcox’s predecessor as United’s director of football, to follow Erik ten Hag after the Dutchman’s sacking in October 2024. Except Wilcox disagreed and Sir Jim Ratcliffe went with Wilcox’s man, Ruben Amorim, and that December Ashworth departed only five months after joining. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Pregnancy does not mean game over’: meet the footballers challenging the myths | Moving the Goalposts
item.description: Claire Emslie and Emma Kelly are among those taking advantage of new research and guidelines for pregnant players Claire Emslie wasn’t expecting to be able to run at 81% of her max speed at 32 weeks pregnant. Emslie, a Scotland international who also plays as a forward for Angel City FC , documented her journey through pregnancy and football training on social media and is part of a growing number of professional female footballers who are getting pregnant in their athletic prime and approaching motherhood with a fresh mindset. Rather than marking the end of a career (notably, Millie Bright announced her pregnancy in September, months after having retired), pregnancy can mark both a continuation and a renewal. Continue reading...

item.title: Less drama, more listening, but is Kozo Tashima the candidate to topple Infantino?
item.description: Japan FA honorary president is hoping a calmer approach that makes fewer unwelcome headlines for Fifa will be welcomed by football Not many remember Japan’s bid for the 2022 World Cup, when the country finished the race with only two of the final 22 votes. Kozo Tashima was involved then, and now the honorary president of the Japan Football Association is going it alone in the hope of ousting Gianni Infantino. The 68-year-old Tashima is an unlikely insurgent and an unlikely challenger to Infantino. He is, however, a familiar and respected figure in Asian and global football politics, and ready to take the Fifa presidency out of the headlines into a quieter era. Continue reading...

item.title: Complaint filed to IRS in relation to Fifa head Gianni Infantino’s housekeeper
item.description: It calls for inquiry into claims she was on Fifa payroll Fifa: Infantino personally pays for ‘any domestic staff’ A complaint has been filed to the United States Internal Revenue Service calling for an investigation into claims an individual on the Fifa payroll was working privately as a housekeeper for Gianni Infantino. If the IRS investigates and finds the claims to be proven then Fifa could lose its tax-exempt status in the US. Fifa has 501(c)(4) status in the country, a category for organisations “created to promote community welfare for charitable, educational or recreational purposes”. Continue reading...

item.title: Which football club has had most international captains in the same team? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. Continue reading...

item.title: Is No 10 still the best, or No 41? The myths and maths of Premier League shirt numbers
item.description: While No 9s still score the most goals and No 1s try to stop them, trends have changed since the introduction of squad numbers in the early 1990s How much is a shirt number worth? It costs £8 if you want two digits added to the back of Arsenal’s 2026-27 home shirt, whereas Manchester City add on £16 for customisation, whether you want a name as well as a number or not. That is cheap compared to what baseball players decide among themselves. Juan Soto bought Brett Baty a $92,000 (£69,000) car in exchange for getting his preferred number (22) when he joined the New York Mets last year. But that’s baseball, where they allow players to wear ‘0’. Anything goes. Continue reading...

item.title: Ultimate 1-50: the male footballers best associated with each squad number
item.description: Who is football’s most legendary No 9? Has there ever been a legendary No 28? And why exactly does Mario Balotelli love wearing No 45 so much? Here’s our list and the stories behind it The relationship between players and numbers is a long-established one filled with memories and fascinating as well as fun stories behind them. With that in mind, the Guardian has had a go at deciding which male player is best associated with each squad number, from 1-50. Various factors were taken into consideration, including how long a player wore/has worn that number, what they achieved/have achieved in it, why they decided to wear it in the first place and, in some cases, how distinctly it has become associated with them in death. The below list is highly subjective and ultimately a bit of fun, but don’t let that stop you being shocked and furious in equal measure. *** Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: That’s a Mora: Rodrigo and Roma rise with Lazio to give Eternal City new life | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Roma and Lazio have both made unbeaten starts to the Serie A season, giving those in the Italian capital dreams of a Scudetto After nine games in 28 days, Gian Piero Gasperini finally got a moment to pause and reflect on Sunday night. The Roma manager was back in Liguria, where he worked for the best part of a decade across two stints at Genoa, to collect an award from Stelle Nello Sport – an association formed to promote sport in the region – celebrating his career achievements and commitment to courageous attacking football. The timing worked out well. Gasperini’s Roma thumped Sassuolo 3-0 on Saturday, bouncing back from a midweek defeat against Manchester United . That result meant the Giallorossi had scored 31 times in 11 Serie A games. In the past 65 years only two Italian teams – the Juventus and Napoli sides of 2017-18 – had made a more prolific start to a top-flight campaign. More importantly, Roma’s victory meant they remained undefeated in domestic competition this season. Just like their neighbours Lazio, who drew 1-1 away against Napoli in the early kick-off on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Felix Nmecha’s faith is forcing Borussia Dortmund into an uncomfortable debate
item.description: Midfielder’s spectacular strikes rescued a frustrating day, only for celebrations to reignite dialogue that has followed him through his career It was just what they needed at just the right time. For a tricky first half and beyond, Elversberg had been a stone in Borussia Dortmund’s shoe, the promoted side not just keeping the home team at bay but keeping them honest, nourishing ambitions of their own. “The fatigue was clearly visible,” the sporting director, Ole Book, said to Sky after a week which had contained Der Klassiker in Munich and a hard-fought Champions League victory against Betis. “We were a bit too focused on managing the game, which was understandable.” Enter Felix Nmecha. BVB have enjoyed a largely excellent start to the season, are unbeaten and level on points with Bayern Munich at the top; Bayern lead, unsurprisingly, thanks to their superior goal difference. It is a gap which has been widened by Dortmund being far from prolific, a facet which looked as if it might undercut their efforts to roll over their visitors on Saturday, especially in the absence of the injured centre-forward Serhou Guirassy. Continue reading...

item.description: The City forward hit a WSL hat-trick for the ninth time while Eva Olid’s United have found defensive stability Not only did Khadija “Bunny” Shaw score a record-extending ninth WSL hat-trick, she scored a “perfect hat-trick” for the fourth time in the competition, something nobody else has managed more than once. Against West Ham the Jamaica striker opened the scoring with her left foot, headed home her second off the underside of the crossbar and tucked in her third with her right foot late on. It helped her side towards a 5-0 win that opened up a two-point gap at the top of the table and stretched Shaw’s lead in the race to be the top division’s top scorer to a five-goal advantage over her nearest challenger, Océane Hurtré. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.dc:creator: Guardian sport
item.content:encoded: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Choke of the century? Chengdu collapse sets up thrilling Chinese Super League climax
item.description: John Aloisi’s players need a point on the final day to seal their maiden title – but their form has dropped off a cliff With four games of the Chinese Super League to go, Chengdu Rongcheng needed just a point to clinch their first title. With one game to go, they still need a point. What was a formality has become a formidable task. The biggest bottle job in Asian football history is very much on and it would be as popular as it would be dramatic. The coach of the Sichuan club, the former Portsmouth and Coventry striker John Aloisi, has seen a 12-point lead over Dalian Yingbo cut to just three before Sunday’s showdowns. Whatever happens, this is a positive and thrilling end to a season that started negatively – literally – with nine of the 16 top-tier clubs kicking off on minus points. Continue reading...

item.title: Rampant Salford hint that Beckham’s lofty ambitions are not a pipe dream
item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. Match-winner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project. Continue reading...

item.title: How can playing for Manchester City fit into Marc Guéhi’s moral universe? | Barney Ronay
item.description: Club’s predicament raises interesting questions about principles, both for individuals and the Premier League I felt unbelievably ponderous. My head was made of Aztec stone. I realised I didn’t want to be with all these people. Somebody came at me, a huge individual in silver and blue. I fell at his feet and grabbed one shoe. I started untying the lace. He kicked away from me. I got up and walked off. I was exceedingly hungry. Not my words. Also not the words of the Manchester City centre-back Marc Guéhi, despite what you were thinking there. This is instead a condensed quote from the mind of Gary Harkness, existentially curious college running-back and the narrator of Don DeLillo’s great American football novel End Zone. Continue reading...

item.title: A phone-free Yellow Wall: are Dortmund urging fans to be present or policing them?
item.description: It makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma By all appearances, things on the Yellow Wall seemed as they always had been. The stadium announcer hollered out the first names of Borussia Dortmund’s starting lineup and the supporters responded with their last names, tens of thousands of voices bellowing as one. Dozens of black and yellow flags waved over Europe’s largest standing terrace, a mass of faces fixed on the field beneath them. And then Signal Iduna Park, sold out with 81,365 fans, roared when Max Beier’s lone goal led Dortmund to victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, putting the home side even on points with Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga standings. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
